issues.title: [Refactor] diffusion/bcg: Share graph-pool output management
issues.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #46659 and #46660. The graph-pool allocation and replay copy logic is repeated across attention wrappers and model-specific breaks. These should share output management without forcing different attention implementations through the same compute path.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `output_factory` to `eager_on_graph`: allocate outputs before ending the captured segment, retain weak references, and validate layouts before replay writeback.
- Allow direct writes through `pass_output=True`, preserving H3 embedding's buffer reuse without copying those tensors into themselves.
- Migrate common diffusion attention, H3/VDN attention, H3 embedding, and Qwen Image 2.1 prefix attention. Ordinary eager execution bypasses the factory and extra copies. Existing calls without a factory retain their current behavior.
- Avoid querying the Ulysses group when USP output prediction does not need SP. Update the BCG documentation.

Production code: 115 lines added, 97 removed across five files. Attention algorithms and backend selection are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on one H200 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 at `66de1dcb7a5e7ec9781f66dd751cffbd085182f5`:

- SRT BCG basic/copy/break-helper, diffusion attention outputs, and LTX tests: **35 passed, 33 subtests passed**.
- Qwen Image 2.1 CPU/CUDA, H3 DiT contract, and VDN suites: **181 passed**. Includes exact padded-prefix replay and direct embedding-buffer checks.
- Small real H3 attention modules with random weights: dense SDPA, VDN full-cover, and VDN partial-window branches each captured two segments and matched eager for five changed-input replays at `rtol=0, atol=0`.
- The standalone LTX USP BCG test fails on the base commit without an initialized SP group and passes with this fix.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Full-checkpoint generation, multi-GPU TP/SP, and AMD/XPU have not been validated in this follow-up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Bounded Qwen prefix-attention microbenchmark, **not full-model E2E**: one H200, BF16, batch 1, 16 heads x 64, SDPA, 128 padded prefix rows, K/V length Q+384. Measures attention plus one output addition. 20 warmups, then median of 9 batches x 200 calls, synchronized on CUDA. Compared against `c43abd6d9e38a14e81bdb77c648a06353e1c10ee`; execution order was new, base, new repeat.

| Q rows | Mode | Base (us) | New, two runs (us) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | eager | 48.90 | 38.16 / 39.10 |
| 256 | BCG | 82.40 | 80.54 / 81.48 |
| 2048 | eager | 75.45 | 71.83 / 72.00 |
| 2048 | BCG | 97.35 | 96.27 / 96.93 |

Output hashes match across commits. Incremental peak PyTorch allocation is unchanged for BCG and lower for eager in both shapes. BCG performance is effectively neutral; eager avoids an unnecessary allocation/copy. No end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Run pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Report correctness and performance evidence with validation limits.
- [x] Follow the existing code style.

issues.title: [Feat] [NPU] qwen-image: Adapt Qwen-Image 2.1 on Ascend
issues.body: Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Qwen-Image-2.1 — adapt the existing SGLang Diffusion pipeline for Ascend*). ## Motivation Qwen-Image 2.1 already runs on Ascend through `torch_npu`, but two hot paths in the DiT stay on the slow eager implementations: `QwenImage21Attention` forces the native fp32 QK RMSNorm on every platform, and the complex RoPE goes through the complex64 multiply path. This PR routes both to the CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`: - `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`. - `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul(..., rotary_mode="interleave")` for the complex RoPE, with the cos/sin tables prepared once per layout and cached. Cos/sin for `npu_rotary_mul` must be expanded with `repeat_interleave(2)`; a plain `cat((c, c), -1)` pairs the wrong frequencies. The previously attempted Triton fast-path enablement on NPU is **not** part of this change: the QK-norm+RoPE Triton kernel is not bit-exact for sequence lengths ≥ 1024 and is 60–95× slower than the eager chain on Ascend. The three kernel files touched by that attempt are restored to their pre-enablement state. The result is full Qwen-Image 2.1 coverage on one A3 chip: text-to-image, single- and multi-reference editing, transparent RGBA output, and local recolor, with NPU CI cases and baselines. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py` - `QwenImage21Attention`: `force_native=not current_platform.is_npu()` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`, so NPU dispatches to `npu_rms_norm` (bit-identical to the native fp32 path in our measurements). - `apply_rope`: NPU branch using `npu_rotary_mul` with cached cos/sin. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/activation/silu_mul_bitexact.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/complex_rope_triton.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_triton.py` - Revert the previous Triton enablement on NPU: restore the CUDA-only guards, drop the `contextlib.nullcontext()` device branch, and remove the added `contextlib` imports. The files are byte-identical to the state before `7e2e7145fa`. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/testcase_configs_npu.py` - Five `qwen_image21_*` NPU cases with the same sampling contract (1024×1024, png, 40 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, `quality="lossless"`): t2i, single-reference edit, two-reference edit, transparent output, and local recolor. - All five set `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit; the t2i case is switched on together with the NPU GT pin in a follow-up commit once the GT-gen workflow has published its image. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json` - Baselines for the five new cases. - `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/prefetch_input_image.py` - Also cache the second multi-image reference and export `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu.yml` - Run the input prefetch before `gen_diffusion_ci_outputs`, so the reference edit cases can produce their published images. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` - `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-2.1.mdx` - Add Ascend to the hardware picker note and the recommended-hardware table (no separate platform section, matching the Qwen-Image cookbook layout). - `docs/src/snippets/configs/Qwen/qwen-image-2.1.jsx` - Add Ascend A3 to the deployment picker: Torch SDPA only, resident placement, `--warmup-mode request`. ## Verification CI cases - All five `qwen_image21_*` cases run end-to-end with `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit, so the PR CI does not depend on a GT that does not exist yet. The recolor case edits the shared TI2I image (orange skirt and bow to deep blue). - Follow-up (same PR, after the GT exists): the `diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu` workflow runs `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu` on the NPU runner and publishes `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu_1gpu.png` to `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/sglang_generated/ascend/` in `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion`. A follow-up commit then enables the t2i consistency check and bumps the NPU `test_utils.py` pin to the returned SHA, in the same commit. **No image is uploaded by hand.** - Both edit inputs are staged by `prefetch_input_image.py` (the shared TI2I image and the second multi-image reference) in `pr-test-npu.yml` and in the GT-generation workflow. `direct_url_test=True` is not used on NPU: it asks the model server to fetch the URLs, while the runner-side prefetch keeps the server offline-capable. - NPU perf baselines for all five cases are in `test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json`, produced on one A3 chip with `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.test.scripts.gen_perf_baselines --case ...` (not hand-written); the existing 13 entries are untouched. ### Reproduction ```bash # t2i sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --prompt "Doraemon is eating dorayaki" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1024 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # ti2i (2D -> 3D) sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --image-path TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg \ --prompt "Convert 2D style to 3D style" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1536 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # multi-image edit (two references; edit2509_1.jpg / edit2509_2.jpg from the # Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@edit2509_1.jpg" -F "image=@edit2509_2.jpg" \ -F "prompt=The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` ```bash # local recolor (CI case): orange skirt and bow -> deep blue curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg" \ -F "prompt=Change the orange skirt and bow to deep blue, keeping her pose, face, hair, and the SGL logo unchanged." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` Transparency is an HTTP generation request with `"background": "transparent"`. The CI recolor case uses `/v1/images/edits` with the shared TI2I image; the transparent-cat recolor below is a separate manual check. ## Accuracy Tests Platform: Ascend A3, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu 2.10.0.post6. Same chip, same seed, `--generator-device cuda` (device RNG, matching the HTTP CI path). Metrics are the repository's consistency metrics (RGB, alpha ignored). ### t2i: A+B (`npu_rms_norm` + `npu_rotary_mul`) vs eager, seeds 42–47 | seed | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | CLIP | mean_abs_diff | max_abs | MSE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 42 | 0.9839 | 30.28 | 0.9983 | 1.716 | 236 | 60.91 | | 43 | 0.9885 | 36.65 | 0.9963 | 1.571 | 139 | 14.05 | | 44 | 0.9881 | 37.43 | 0.9968 | 1.216 | 95 | 11.76 | | 45 | 0.9777 | 30.58 | 0.9947 | 2.225 | 248 | 56.91 | | 46 | 0.9695 | 28.91 | 0.9903 | 3.140 | 223 | 83.55 | | 47 | 0.9711 | 27.18 | 0.9901 | 3.169 | 219 | 124.34 | Repository thresholds: CLIP ≥ 0.92, SSIM ≥ 0.95, PSNR ≥ 28 dB, mean_abs_diff ≤ 8. All six seeds pass CLIP and mean_abs_diff; five of six pass SSIM; seed 47 is 0.82 dB below the PSNR threshold (mean_abs_diff 3.17, well inside). Visual inspection: the subject, shape and colors are preserved; differences are pixel-level. ### ti2i: 2D → 3D style conversion (A+B) Input is the shared CI edit image `TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg` (sha256 `0d56a63fca6ef8fe2a0ca27a0774c2bada9b2a198aeedbfdfb23bec09d0d3901`), prompt `Convert 2D style to 3D style`, seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1. End-to-end on one A3 chip (A+B, `quality="lossless"`): 23.1 s at 1024×1024 (denoise 16.69 s, 0.417 s/step, decode 2.79 s) and 36.8 s at 1536×1024 (denoise 28.25 s, 0.706 s/step, decode 4.74 s). ### multi-image editing (A+B) Two reference images (`edit2509_1.jpg` magician bear, `edit2509_2.jpg` alchemist bear, from the Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set), sent as two `image` fields to HTTP `/v1/images/edits`; seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1, 1024×1024, `quality="lossless"`. The server log confirms the request carries both paths. - **Composition** — with the multi-image CI prompt ("The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square."), both identities are preserved (hat/robe/book/wand, graduation cap/cauldron/fan/Qwen shirt) and placed as instructed. - **Slot binding** — with "the bear from image 1 … image 2 …", uploading `[ref1, ref2]` puts ref1 on the left and ref2 on the right; uploading `[ref2, ref1]` swaps them. The second file lands in ``; it is not silently dropped or merged into the first. - **Ablation** — one reference at a time produces only that subject. - **Determinism** — repeating the request, or running it on a different chip, reproduces a byte-identical PNG. The CI case uses the two references staged for the NPU runner (the shared TI2I image and `rabbit.jpg`); the bear pair above is the manual slot-binding check. | request | CLIP | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | mean_abs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | official (2 refs, CI prompt) | 0.9793 | 0.8285 | 17.78 | 10.182 | | order [1,2] | 0.9983 | 0.9631 | 26.58 | 1.972 | | order [2,1] | 0.9913 | 0.8986 | 21.39 | 5.811 | | ref 1 only | 0.9995 | 0.9947 | 39.80 | 0.666 | | ref 2 only | 0.9986 | 0.9768 | 25.97 | 1.992 | Differences vs eager concentrate on anti-aliased outlines and glyphs, with no structural or identity change (the amplified diff maps are edge-only). A two-reference request carries a 2×4096-token condition prefix, so the same tiny operator-level rounding differences are amplified relative to the single-reference case; CLIP stays ≥ 0.979. The edit case has no GT (`run_consistency_check=False`), so these numbers are supplementary evidence, not a consistency gate. ### Local recolor (A+B, CI case) Input is the shared TI2I image; the prompt changes the orange skirt and bow to deep blue, keeping the pose, face, hair, and SGL logo unchanged. ### RGBA / transparency (A+B) Prompt: an isolated cat on a transparent background, with `background="transparent"` and `output_format="png"`. | | alpha min/max | alpha mean | alpha<250 | alpha<128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | eager | 0 / 255 | 83.62 | 69.13% | 67.20% | | A+B | 0 / 255 | 83.70 | 69.11% | 67.17% | - alpha MAE 0.117, alpha max diff 32, transparent-mask IoU 0.9993 - RGB SSIM 0.9976, PSNR 46.70 dB The model does produce a meaningful alpha channel (~69% transparent pixels); A+B preserves it almost exactly. ### Manual check: transparent cat recolor with alpha (A+B) This is a separate manual check, not the CI recolor case above. issues.title: [Doc] diffusion: add Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S) recipe for Qwen-Image 2.1
issues.body:
### Summary

Adds a measured recipe for the AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, gfx1151) to the Qwen-Image 2.1 cookbook: one row in the hardware table and a `### Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S)` subsection next to the existing DGX Spark one.

The subsection records two platform prerequisites that are not obvious from the existing AMD guidance:

- `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1` — a **PyTorch** SDPA switch, not an SGLang flag. Without it PyTorch falls back from the Flash-efficient attention kernel and 1024x1024/40-step latency goes from ~155 s to more than 9 minutes on this GPU (measured).
- `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` — the runtime resolves the backend to AITER by default, which is not verified on gfx1151.

### Measurement

Same methodology as the existing table: original checkpoint, 1024x1024, 40 steps, CFG 1, one RGBA PNG per request, median HTTP latency of three warm requests after a discarded warmup, excluding startup. Peak memory is the request-phase sample reported by the server.

| Config | Median | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch_sdpa` + AOTriton env (row value) | 154.98 s | 3 runs: 154.93 / 154.98 / 155.11 |
| `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true` (default MC=3) | 56.96 s | documented as an optional speed/fidelity trade |

Platform: Ubuntu 24.04.2, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, PyTorch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4 (HIP 7.2.53211), Radeon 8060S with 128 GB unified memory (the kernel reports a 512 MiB VRAM carve-out, GTT cap ~108 GiB). FP8 is unavailable on this GPU.

### Scope and limits

- Only numbers reproducible on **upstream main with merged features** are used. Custom Triton kernels from open PRs (#44037 / #46065 / #46515) are intentionally excluded, so the row is slower than our best local result.
- **Edit** is left as `—`: `POST /v1/images/edits` returns 500 with `prompt_embeds ... NaN` on this base checkpoint, and `Qwen-Image-Edit-2511` weights are not available on the test machine. Transparent output is likewise unverified.
- Cache-DiT quality: PSNR 28.4 dB at default settings vs 27.5 dB with `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_MC=6`, measured with the CLI on the same prompt and seed.

### Checklist

- [x] Only `docs/` changed; no code or CI changes
- [x] Follows `docs/AGENTS.md` (platform/OS/version stated, no guessed defaults, copy-pasteable commands)
- [x] Latency stated with the same definition as the existing table
- [x] Unverified items marked explicitly (`—`, "remain unverified")

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion model: Accelerate conditioning hashing with GPU BLAKE3
issues.body:
## Motivation

This PR follows up on [#46028](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46028), extending the GPU hash optimization introduced for Cosmos3 to other diffusion models with suitable conditioning workloads.

Profiling shows that hashing large visual conditioning tensors adds substantial device-to-host transfers and CPU SHA-256 work before VAE or vision encoding. Reusing the existing GPU [BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) implementation keeps tensor-content hashing on the GPU and returns only the 32-byte digest to the CPU.

## Modifications

- Add `use_gpu_conditioning_hash()` to select GPU hashing within an existing conditioning-cache scope. CPU tensors use the original digest, and nested scopes restore the previous policy on exit, including exceptions.
- Reuse `gpu_tensor_blake3` from `python/sglang/kernels/ops/memory/gpu_tensor_hash_blake3.py`. Keep `_fingerprint`'s signature and container recursion; select the digest only in its Tensor branch.
- Enable the policy at these conditioning paths:

| Path | Models |
| --- | --- |
| Ref2VA VAE and vision-encoder inputs | MiniMax-H3, FastH3-Omni |
| Control/reference-video VAE inputs | Cosmos3 Transfer, Cosmos3 multiview and Simulation, Wan2.2-Animate-2 including Distilled |
| Multiple reference images | FLUX.2/Klein and Qwen-Image-Edit through the shared image-VAE stage; Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE and vision encoding; GLM-Image VAE |
| Video-clip memory VAE inputs | JoyAI-Echo |

**Workload selection matters.** The shared `ImageVAEEncodingStage` opts in only when `num_frames == 1 and len(images) > 1`. These are multiple reference images without padded zero frames; images are still hashed and encoded individually. Ordinary I2V inputs contain one image followed by zero frames, and the original digest already filters nonzero blocks on the GPU to avoid transferring the padding. Single-image requests keep the default policy in this stage.

The scoped policy can be reused at other conditioning-cache call sites. Further single-image or model-specific adoption should be based on the actual tensor size, sparsity, and measured hash cost.

## Accuracy Tests

- All 11 completed comparisons for newly adapted workloads produced **bitwise-identical decoded RGB frames and audio samples where present**. The existing Cosmos3 V2V reference comparison also passed.
- GPU digests matched the standard CPU BLAKE3 implementation for the tested conditioning tensors.
- Current cache, model-boundary, and text-encoding regressions: **130 passed, 1 skipped**. Coverage includes CPU fallback, content changes, nested scopes, exception restoration, and posterior sampling/RNG. Pre-commit passed.
- Full-model validation remains pending for JoyAI-Echo, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, and GLM-Image. They are integrated but excluded from the performance table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB; Xeon Platinum 8480+ with 16 logical CPUs; SGLang Docker `b1259f3ea327`.

Each mode runs in a separate process on the same GPU: one complete warmup followed by one measured request, using different visual inputs and prompts to avoid warmup cache hits. The baseline retains the original digest, including GPU zero-block filtering; other settings are identical within each pair.

Hash timing includes tensor-content hashing and required transfers with inputs ready, and excludes VAE encoding and upstream waits. E2E includes generation and output saving, excluding model loading. Speedup is original time divided by GPU-hash time.

Outputs: MiniMax/FastH3 896×512, 107 frames; Wan-Animate 576×1024 with a requested 37-frame clip; Cosmos3 832×480, 45 frames per view; Klein 1024×1024. MiniMax uses layerwise offload with 20 DiT layers resident; FastH3 uses Torch SDPA on SM120.

| Workload | Original hash (ms) | GPU hash (ms) | Hash speedup | Original E2E (s) | GPU-hash E2E (s) | E2E speedup | Original hash / E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MiniMax-H3: video, 50 steps | 1743.327 | 23.729 | 73.47× | 930.811 | 937.821 | 0.993× | 0.187% |

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Hash large conditioning-cache keys in parallel chunks
issues.body:
## Motivation

The conditioning cache keys every encoder call by a SHA-256 of its inputs, and computes the key before it knows whether the call will hit. For an image-conditioned request every key misses on new inputs, so hashing is pure request-path cost. One Qwen-Image-2.1 edit with a 1024x704 reference (resized to 1248x864) hashes three copies of the image:

| key | bytes | time, before |
|---|---|---|
| VAE input (`AutoencoderKLQwenImage21.encode`, after a GPU→CPU copy) | 8.6 MB | 10.1 ms |
| text encoder outer key (the resized PIL image) | 4.3 MB | 3.6 ms |
| vision tower (`_get_flat_visual_features`, processor output after a GPU→CPU copy) | 25.9 MB | 19.9 ms |

(1xH200, server timings around each key.) These run on the host before the vision tower is launched, while the GPU has only the VAE encode to do, so they add almost one to one to the request. Single-threaded `hashlib.sha256` runs at about 1.45 GB/s on the host CPU.

The cache is kept. It is exact, and it serves repeated inputs: the same reference with a new prompt reuses the VAE latents and the vision features, and the same request with a new seed skips the encoders. Only the key gets cheaper.

## Modifications

`runtime/cache/conditioning.py`: `_digest` hashes a buffer of at most 2 MiB with SHA-256 as before. A larger buffer is hashed as SHA-256 over its length and the SHA-256 digests of its 2 MiB chunks. The chunks are hashed on a module-level thread pool of up to eight threads; `hashlib` releases the GIL while it hashes. The digest still covers every byte and keeps SHA-256's collision resistance. Tensors (dense and sparse block paths), PIL images and NumPy arrays use it.

Measured on one host core vs eight threads: a 25 MB buffer takes 16.9 ms with one SHA-256 and 2.3 ms chunked.

Tests: `test_conditioning_cache.py::test_chunked_input_digest_covers_every_byte` sends inputs larger than a chunk through the real cache (a VAE encode and a PIL image key): an equal copy hits; a change in the first byte, at a chunk boundary, in the last element, or in the length misses.

## Accuracy Tests

Keys change format, values do not: a hit returns the stored output as before, and a miss computes it as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024 with the harness's request (distinct inputs per request, so every key misses), measured inside one server that switches between chunked and single-threaded hashing request by request (interleaved rounds; an A/A pair in the same rotation stays within 5 ms):

| | single-threaded keys | this PR | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1xH200, 8 rounds | 5.177 s | 5.155 s | −22 ms |
| 1xB300, 6 rounds | 2.624 s | 2.603 s | −17 ms |

With this PR, turning the whole conditioning cache off saves only another 13 ms on H200 (it was 39 ms on main), which is what repeated-input users now pay for their hits.

issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: add a Triton dense attention prefill path for gfx1151
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (Ryzen AI MAX 395, gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off: only gfx1151 has been measured. gfx11 should behave the
  same, gfx9x untested — flip the default once there are numbers.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above, not a derived bound: the kernel alone
  is faster at every length, but the three head-major materialisations dominate
  short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's FFN activation fast path (fused_silu_mul_bitexact) is gated on current_platform.is_cuda(). On ROCm that predicate is False (PlatformEnum.ROCM), so the optimization is dead code on AMD hardware — even though the fused kernel is plain Triton (no CUDA JIT / PTX) and reproduces the eager silu(a) * b chain bit-exactly on HIP.

This is the same situation the XPU port fixed in #41940, which enabled the identical kernel via (x.is_cuda or x.is_xpu). This PR does the equivalent for ROCm/HIP.

Modifications

  • Add _silu_mul_device = current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_hip().

  • Gate QwenImage21FeedForward.forward on _silu_mul_device instead of the vendor-pure _is_cuda.

Every other fast path in the module (RoPE, QK-norm, packed QKV, SDPA) stays CUDA-only, because those really are CUDA JIT / PTX kernels. issues.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46429. `resolve_sequential_cfg` decides between packed and sequential CFG from each rank's own free memory ([L159](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/flux3_image.py#L159)). The two paths issue different TP all-reduces and SP exchanges per step, so when the ranks decide differently their collectives no longer match, and the request hangs or fails (details in the issue).

## Modifications

- Take the MIN of free memory over the TP and SP groups before comparing, as `_cache_fits` already does in the Qwen-Image 2.1 stage ([L351-L358](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/qwen_image21.py#L351-L358)).
- New test `test_sequential_cfg_is_agreed_across_ranks` in `test_flux3_image_stages.py` runs two CPU ranks, once as TP=2 and once as Ulysses SP=2, with rank 1 reporting 1 MiB free, and checks that both ranks choose sequential CFG. On main both subtests fail with `AssertionError: [False, True]`; with this change the file passes.

## Accuracy Tests

2x H200, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base` (base e262b44), TP=2, 2048x2048, 20 steps, with another process holding memory on GPU 1 only so that the ranks would split. Without this change the request got no response for 300 s; with it, both ranks chose sequential CFG and the request completed. Two runs with the change gave bit-identical images, and they are also bit-identical to the output without the change when memory is held on both GPUs, so that both ranks take the sequential path.

Not measured. The change adds at most two CPU all-reduces of one int64 per denoise call, before the step loop.

## Motivation

`BaseLayerWithLoRA` keeps its disabled/merged pass-through eager and compiles only the dynamic adapter path, because layerwise offload can rebind weights. `LinearWithLoRA` instead decorates its entire `forward` with `torch.compile`: wrapping an ordinary `nn.Linear` changes the base dispatch even when no adapter is active or after it is disabled. Compilers may choose a different GEMM/bias fusion; this also defeats the shared class's offload precaution.

The AMD Qwen Image 2.1 LoRA tests in [this run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37030627223/job/110916375120) fail exact base-output restoration by 1.1920928955078125e-7. - Mirror `BaseLayerWithLoRA`: directly invoke the original base layer when disabled or merged, and apply merged output offsets eagerly when present.
- Keep compilation on the active dynamic LoRA path.
- Add disabled/merged × absent/present offset coverage, exact output checks and repeated weight rebinds. A compiler-sensitive value witness verifies that the pass-through really uses eager dispatch (a Python assertion alone can graph-break and miss this regression).

issues.body:
## Motivation

Allow native SGLang Diffusion pipelines to use a single-file Tiny AutoEncoder
checkpoint for approximate image and video reconstruction. This provides an
optional lightweight final decoder while preserving the original VAE encoder
and latent metadata for conditioning inputs.

The existing FLUX.2 Tiny AutoEncoder component override remains available.

## Modifications

- Add `--tiny-vae-model` and `--tiny-vae-path`, with matching Python pipeline
  configuration fields. Reject incomplete option pairs and the Diffusers backend.
- Add MIT-licensed TAESD and TAEHV network implementations covering SD/SDXL,
  SD3, FLUX.1, FLUX.2, Qwen Image 2.1, HunyuanVideo, Wan2.1/2.2,
  HunyuanVideo 1.5, MiniMax-H3, and LTX-2 architectures. Accept ComfyUI video
  checkpoint names as aliases. Architecture support does not add generation
  pipelines for models that SGLang does not already support.
- Load full or decoder-only tensor state dictionaries from safetensors or
  PyTorch checkpoints through the existing weight resolver. Validate decoder
  keys strictly and reuse the configured VAE decode precision.

issues.title: [diffusion] quantization: packed Q/K/V projection for convrot_int8's comfy_kitchen backend
issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's QwenImage21Attention projects Q/K/V from one activation with three separate [C, C] linears. convrot_int8 has two kernel backends:

  • the JIT / customkernel backend (CC 9.0 / 10.0 / 12.0 / 12.1), which #38040 already gives a fused single rotation + activation quantisation for q/k/v sharing one input;

  • the comfy_kitchen backend, which serves the GPUs the JIT ops do not build for (CC 8.x Ampere/Ada, CC 10.3) and has no equivalent: every attention block pays two redundant ConvRot activation quantisations and issues three narrow GEMMs.

On a GPU with no FP8/NVFP4 tensor cores -- A100 (CC 8.0), RTX 30/40-series -- the comfy_kitchen backend is not a fallback, it is the only INT8 path, so this gap is real there.

Modifications

  1. layers/quantization/convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py: the fused kernel apply ran inline moves to a module-level int8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, group_size, bias=None, split_out_features=None), and apply becomes a thin adapter. This is a pure refactor: the op, its argument order and its numerics are unchanged, and there is now a single place for the row-split cap. split_out_features lets a packed caller judge the row-split heuristic on the per-projection width instead of the packed width.

  2. models/dits/qwen_image21.py: teach the existing bf16 packing to also cover convrot_int8. The three int8 [C, C] weights and the matching [C, 1] fp32 row scales are re-homed onto one [3C, C] / [3C, 1] storage each, and _project_qkv_packed_convrot_int8 projects all three through a single int8_linear call. A new BitExactFusionGate verifies the first call against the module forwards and falls back on any mismatch, so the packed path can only ever be used when it is bit-exact.

  3. test/unit/test_qwen_image21.py: four new unit tests -- storage sharing keeps values and shares one storage; the packing predicate requires the convrot_int8 method; the consecutive-slice view rejects gaps and separate storages; the packed int8_linear call is bit-exact against the separate per-projection calls at production shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Packed call is bit-exact against the separate calls (max_abs = 0.0); cat(quantize(W_i)) equals quantize(cat(W_i)) exactly. End-to-end on A100 GPU 0 (1024x1024, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42), the output PNG md5 is identical to the frozen INT8 baseline: 05288a62012b1353230d53c3297cb67c. The whole flow is inside the existing bit-exact gate, so an unexpected mismatch disables the fusion rather than changing the output.

Speed Tests and Profiling

A100 GPU 0 (CC 8.0, comfy_kitchen backend), Qwen-Image 2.1, 1024x1024 @ 40 steps, CFG 1:

arm | denoise | per step | output md5 -- | -- | -- | -- convrot_int8, unpacked QKV | 9.059 s | -- | 05288a62... convrot_int8, packed QKV (this PR) | 8.796 s | 0.220 s | 05288a62...

Kernel level (M=4114, C=4096, group_size=256): 1.263 ms -> 1.005 ms per attention block (-0.257 ms/block, -8.2 ms/step); the whole saving is the removed ConvRot work.

Scope: on JIT-capable GPUs (H100/H200/Blackwell) the equivalent fusion already exists via the customkernel backend, so this PR is a backend-parity change with no effect there.

  • Format your code according to the pre-commit guide.

  • Add unit tests.

  • Update documentation / docstrings as needed.

  • Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

issues.title: [diffusion] cache: add DPCache, calibrated key-timestep caching
issues.body:
## Motivation

This PR adds DPCache, training-free key-timestep caching driven by an offline-calibrated schedule. It adapts [Denoising as Path Planning: Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion Models with DPCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22654); the algorithm is credited to that paper.

A request carries a schedule of `K` full steps. Those steps run the whole transformer block stack. On every other step, DPCache extrapolates the final block feature from the two most recent full steps and runs only the output head, using the current timestep. Every scheduler update still runs and the weights are unchanged, so this is approximate inference, not distillation or a reduced-step sampler.

On Qwen-Image 2.1 (1024x1024, 40 steps, one RTX 5090), `K=20` is **1.97x faster end to end** with mean LPIPS 0.0076 against native output. That is 10.9% less time than the conservative Cache-DiT preset, with lower mean and max LPIPS. `K=12` is **3.21x faster**.

DPCache plugs in the same way as Spectrum and TeaCache: a mixin on `CachableDiT`. Any DiT can opt in; Qwen-Image 2.1 is the first. A schedule is calibrated per deployment, so the server owns the schedules and a request only picks a budget. A calibration tool builds the schedules.

```bash
# 1. calibrate once per checkpoint and request configuration
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate record --model-path MODEL \
  --prompts-file prompts.txt --height 1024 --width 1024 --num-inference-steps 40 \
  --capture-dir captures
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate plan \
  --capture-dir captures --budgets 12 20 --out-dir schedules
# 2. serve; requests pick a budget with dpcache_budget, or use the default
sglang serve --model-path MODEL --dpcache-schedule-dir schedules --dpcache-default-budget 20
```

## Modifications

- `runtime/cache/dpcache.py`: a BF16 first-order predictor and per-request, per-CFG-branch state. Also PACT calibration costs, an exact DP planner over anchor pairs, and a versioned JSON schedule. The schedule records the checkpoint, scheduler class and config, timesteps and sigmas, resolution, guidance, attention backend and dtype, and a request that doesn't match it is rejected before denoising.
- Schedules belong to the deployment. `--dpcache-schedule-dir` loads the schedules a server serves and checks them against its pipeline, checkpoint and attention backend at startup, so a schedule built for another deployment fails the launch. A request sets `dpcache_budget: K` and the server picks the schedule with that budget calibrated for the request's resolution, step count, scheduler, guidance and dtype. If none fits, the request fails. `--dpcache-default-budget` applies to requests that set no budget and falls back to native where no schedule fits, and `dpcache_budget: 0` opts a request out. `sglang generate --dpcache-budget` and the image/video APIs (extra field) accept the budget.
- `DPCacheMixin` on `CachableDiT`: to opt in, a model sets `_supports_dpcache = True` and routes its block stack through `self.dpcache_blocks(run_blocks)`. The output head stays outside the callable. The model takes no extra arguments; the hook reads the current step and the branch's state from the forward context.
- `DenoisingStage.forward`: checks scope, selects the schedule, attaches fresh state for each CFG branch (`Req.dpcache_states`), and clears it after success or failure. Requests that use no budget take the native path unchanged. A requested budget outside the supported scope fails explicitly; only the server default falls back to native.
- DPCache requests are excluded from dynamic batching: a merged request carries several prompts, and DPCache is calibrated for one. Warmup requests run natively because they use fewer steps than any calibrated schedule.
- Qwen-Image 2.1: `_supports_dpcache = True`, and the block loop moves into `_forward_blocks` without changes.
- Calibration tool (second commit), `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate`:
  - `record` runs a prompts file natively with the new `dpcache_calibration` request field. The worker scores prediction errors online from each step's final block feature and writes one small capture per prompt; features never leave the worker. It can be sharded across GPUs and resumed.
  - `plan` averages the captures and writes one `K{n}.json` schedule per budget into the directory the server serves.
  - Online and offline scoring share one routine. `dpcache_calibration` writes a file on the worker, so the HTTP APIs do not accept it.
  - Also in this commit: the worker bootstrap's early-import warning no longer reports namespace packages. They run no code, and `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.<tool>` imports `sglang.multimodal_gen.tools` in every spawned child.
- Docs: `dpcache.mdx` covers scope, the schedule format, the calibration API and how to add a model, and it is listed in the caching overview.

Supported scope for now: BF16, single-image text-to-image, one GPU, eager execution. The following are rejected: CFG, reference images, LoRA, dual-transformer models, torch compile or CUDA graphs, SP/TP/CFG parallelism, and combining DPCache with Cache-DiT, TeaCache, Spectrum, skip-softmax or attention-backend overrides. No calibrated schedule ships with this PR, because a schedule is bound to one checkpoint and request configuration. Operators build one per configuration with the calibration tool.

Review feedback is especially welcome on the serving API (server-owned schedules plus a per-request budget) and on the mixin hook as the integration point for more models.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_dpcache.py`, `test_dpcache_calibrate.py` and the DPCache cases in `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: **158 passed**. The related regression tests (Qwen-Image 2.1, sampling params, SenseNova-U1 scheduler batching, Spectrum, MiniMax-H3 denoise loop, worker bootstrap, layerwise offload, server args), each file run on its own: **559 passed**. All of these ran on the current head, rebased onto `abef3efb6`.
- Requests without DPCache produce output identical to upstream `1d59ce7c9` (checked before the rebase): 8/8 final latents, decoded tensors and PNG bytes match on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint.
- End to end on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint:
  - The calibration tool, run on the 10 calibration prompts behind the schedules measured below, reproduced them exactly: identical full steps and calibrated costs for every budget from `K=12` to `K=39`. Recording took 2 min 53 s on one RTX 5090 including model load, and the 10 captures total 5 MB.
  - Serving those schedules from `--dpcache-schedule-dir` on the current head reproduced the measured held-out outputs bit for bit on 9 of 9 requests: `K=20` through the server default, `K=12` requested explicitly, and native through `dpcache_budget: 0`.
  - With the default budget, a 768x768 request (no schedule) ran natively. The same request with an explicit `K=20` was rejected with the available schedules listed.
- Quality with a schedule is reported in the table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: Qwen-Image 2.1 BF16 (revision `790c9263`), 1x RTX 5090 32 GB, torch 2.13, 1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0, `torch_sdpa`, eager, DiT layerwise offload. DPCache schedules were calibrated on 10 prompts, `K` was selected on 8 different prompts, and the Cache-DiT presets were tuned on those same 8. Every choice was frozen before one measurement on 20 fresh held-out prompt/seed pairs. The prompt sets are disjoint.

| Config | Transformer blocks / image | DenoisingStage | E2E | E2E speedup | LPIPS mean / max | PSNR mean / min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| native | 1280 | 13.26 s | 13.46 s | 1.00x | - | - |
| **DPCache `K=20`** | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | **1.97x** | **0.0076 / 0.035** | **41.5 / 28.2 dB** |
| Cache-DiT conservative | 710 | 7.47 s | 7.68 s | 1.75x | 0.0159 / 0.042 | 38.1 / 27.8 dB |
| uniform `K=20` (ablation) | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | 1.97x | 0.070 / 0.208 | 28.3 / 17.2 dB |
| **DPCache `K=12`** | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | **3.21x** | **0.085** / 0.220 | **27.6** / 17.1 dB |
| Cache-DiT stock | 443 | 4.77 s | 4.98 s | 2.71x | 0.102 / 0.176 | 26.2 / 20.7 dB |
| uniform `K=12` (ablation) | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | 3.21x | 0.155 / 0.280 | 22.3 / 16.2 dB |

- The two Cache-DiT rows are two settings of the same method. **Stock** is SGLang's Cache-DiT default (`residual_diff_threshold=0.24`, `max_warmup_steps=4`, `max_continuous_cached_steps=3`, `Fn=1`, `Bn=0`). **Conservative** is a stricter preset we picked on the 8 validation prompts to meet a mean/max LPIPS gate of 0.05/0.10 (`residual_diff_threshold=0.12`, `max_warmup_steps=10`, `max_continuous_cached_steps=1`, `Fn=1`, `Bn=1`).
- Each DPCache budget is compared with the Cache-DiT setting of similar quality. `K=20` takes 10.9% less time than conservative Cache-DiT and is closer to native on every quality column. Stock Cache-DiT is faster than `K=20` but much further from native. `K=12` takes 15.6% less time than stock Cache-DiT and has the better mean, but a worse worst case (LPIPS max 0.220 vs 0.176).
- The uniform ablations keep DPCache's budget, first three steps and last full step, and spread the other full steps evenly. They take the same time and are clearly further from native, so the gain comes from the calibrated placement, not only from the budget.
- DenoisingStage is device time averaged over the 20 held-out images. E2E is client wall-clock for a warm generation (encode, denoise, decode, offload transfers), from interleaved paired runs over 4 held-out prompts. Speedup is the paired mean.
- LPIPS (AlexNet) and PSNR compare each image with the native output for the same prompt and seed, after compositing on white.
- With layerwise offload, predicted steps loaded no block weights, and peak memory rose by 154 MB (0.6%). Time scales almost linearly with `K`, because a predicted step costs only the per-step preparation and the output head.
- A low mean LPIPS does not guarantee that every image is preserved. `K=12` rearranged the chairs in a counting prompt and changed the lettering on a sign. `K=20` stayed visually close on every held-out pair.
- One-time cost: about 3 GPU-minutes of calibration per checkpoint and request configuration (10 prompts), plus choosing `K` on a separate validation set.

The benchmark harnesses, frozen corpora, published schedules, the full report and worst-case galleries are in [`fractalyze/sglang@experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache`](https://github.com/fractalyze/sglang/tree/experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache/benchmark/experiments/qwen_image21_dpcache). That branch is not part of this PR. It stacks on an earlier revision of this PR (`2754e6ecf`) that passed the schedule with each request. The inference path is the same, and the served-schedule outputs above are bit-identical to those measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint changed code.
- [x] Add unit and CUDA tests for the hook, stage lifecycle, schedule loading and selection, scope checks, batching exclusion, warmup and calibration.
- [x] Update usage and scope documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results on the current code.
- [ ] Complete maintainer review and upstream CI before merging.

issues.body: Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Qwen-Image-2.1 — adapt the existing SGLang Diffusion pipeline for Ascend*). ## Motivation Qwen-Image 2.1 already runs on Ascend through `torch_npu`, but two hot paths in the DiT stay on the slow eager implementations: `QwenImage21Attention` forces the native fp32 QK RMSNorm on every platform, and the complex RoPE goes through the complex64 multiply path. This PR routes both to the CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`: - `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`. - `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul(..., rotary_mode="interleave")` for the complex RoPE, with the cos/sin tables prepared once per layout and cached. Cos/sin for `npu_rotary_mul` must be expanded with `repeat_interleave(2)`; a plain `cat((c, c), -1)` pairs the wrong frequencies. The previously attempted Triton fast-path enablement on NPU is **not** part of this change: the QK-norm+RoPE Triton kernel is not bit-exact for sequence lengths ≥ 1024 and is 60–95× slower than the eager chain on Ascend. The three kernel files touched by that attempt are restored to their pre-enablement state. The result is full Qwen-Image 2.1 coverage on one A3 chip: text-to-image, single- and multi-reference editing, transparent RGBA output, and local recolor, with NPU CI cases and baselines. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py` - `QwenImage21Attention`: `force_native=not current_platform.is_npu()` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`, so NPU dispatches to `npu_rms_norm` (bit-identical to the native fp32 path in our measurements). - `apply_rope`: NPU branch using `npu_rotary_mul` with cached cos/sin. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/activation/silu_mul_bitexact.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/complex_rope_triton.py`, `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/rope/qknorm_complex_rope_triton.py` - Revert the previous Triton enablement on NPU: restore the CUDA-only guards, drop the `contextlib.nullcontext()` device branch, and remove the added `contextlib` imports. The files are byte-identical to the state before `7e2e7145fa`. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/testcase_configs_npu.py` - Five `qwen_image21_*` NPU cases with the same sampling contract (1024×1024, png, 40 steps, guidance 1, seed 42, `quality="lossless"`): t2i, single-reference edit, two-reference edit, transparent output, and local recolor. - All five set `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit; the t2i case is switched on together with the NPU GT pin in a follow-up commit once the GT-gen workflow has published its image. - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json` - Baselines for the five new cases. - `scripts/ci/utils/diffusion/prefetch_input_image.py` - Also cache the second multi-image reference and export `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `.github/workflows/diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu.yml` - Run the input prefetch before `gen_diffusion_ci_outputs`, so the reference edit cases can produce their published images. - `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` - `SGLANG_TEST_MULTI_IMAGE_INPUT_IMAGE`. - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Qwen-Image/Qwen-Image-2.1.mdx` - Add Ascend to the hardware picker note and the recommended-hardware table (no separate platform section, matching the Qwen-Image cookbook layout). - `docs/src/snippets/configs/Qwen/qwen-image-2.1.jsx` - Add Ascend A3 to the deployment picker: Torch SDPA only, resident placement, `--warmup-mode request`. ## Verification CI cases - All five `qwen_image21_*` cases run end-to-end with `run_consistency_check=False` in this commit, so the PR CI does not depend on a GT that does not exist yet. The recolor case edits the shared TI2I image (orange skirt and bow to deep blue). - Follow-up (same PR, after the GT exists): the `diffusion-ci-gt-gen-npu` workflow runs `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu` on the NPU runner and publishes `qwen_image21_t2i_1npu_1gpu.png` to `diffusion-ci/consistency_gt/sglang_generated/ascend/` in `sgl-project/ci-data-diffusion`. A follow-up commit then enables the t2i consistency check and bumps the NPU `test_utils.py` pin to the returned SHA, in the same commit. **No image is uploaded by hand.** - Both edit inputs are staged by `prefetch_input_image.py` (the shared TI2I image and the second multi-image reference) in `pr-test-npu.yml` and in the GT-generation workflow. `direct_url_test=True` is not used on NPU: it asks the model server to fetch the URLs, while the runner-side prefetch keeps the server offline-capable. - NPU perf baselines for all five cases are in `test/server/ascend/perf_baselines_npu.json`, produced on one A3 chip with `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.test.scripts.gen_perf_baselines --case ...` (not hand-written); the existing 13 entries are untouched. ### Reproduction ```bash # t2i sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --prompt "Doraemon is eating dorayaki" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1024 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # ti2i (2D -> 3D) sglang generate --model-path /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 \ --image-path TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg \ --prompt "Convert 2D style to 3D style" \ --num-inference-steps 40 --guidance-scale 1 \ --height 1536 --width 1024 --seed 42 --num-gpus 1 \ --generator-device cuda --save-output ``` ```bash # multi-image edit (two references; edit2509_1.jpg / edit2509_2.jpg from the # Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@edit2509_1.jpg" -F "image=@edit2509_2.jpg" \ -F "prompt=The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` ```bash # local recolor (CI case): orange skirt and bow -> deep blue curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits \ -F "model=/path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1" \ -F "image=@TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg" \ -F "prompt=Change the orange skirt and bow to deep blue, keeping her pose, face, hair, and the SGL logo unchanged." \ -F "size=1024x1024" -F "num_inference_steps=40" -F "guidance_scale=1" \ -F "seed=42" -F "quality=lossless" -F "response_format=b64_json" ``` Transparency is an HTTP generation request with `"background": "transparent"`. The CI recolor case uses `/v1/images/edits` with the shared TI2I image; the transparent-cat recolor below is a separate manual check. ## Accuracy Tests Platform: Ascend A3, CANN 9.1.0, torch 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu 2.10.0.post6. Same chip, same seed, `--generator-device cuda` (device RNG, matching the HTTP CI path). Metrics are the repository's consistency metrics (RGB, alpha ignored). ### t2i: A+B (`npu_rms_norm` + `npu_rotary_mul`) vs eager, seeds 42–47 | seed | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | CLIP | mean_abs_diff | max_abs | MSE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 42 | 0.9839 | 30.28 | 0.9983 | 1.716 | 236 | 60.91 | | 43 | 0.9885 | 36.65 | 0.9963 | 1.571 | 139 | 14.05 | | 44 | 0.9881 | 37.43 | 0.9968 | 1.216 | 95 | 11.76 | | 45 | 0.9777 | 30.58 | 0.9947 | 2.225 | 248 | 56.91 | | 46 | 0.9695 | 28.91 | 0.9903 | 3.140 | 223 | 83.55 | | 47 | 0.9711 | 27.18 | 0.9901 | 3.169 | 219 | 124.34 | Repository thresholds: CLIP ≥ 0.92, SSIM ≥ 0.95, PSNR ≥ 28 dB, mean_abs_diff ≤ 8. All six seeds pass CLIP and mean_abs_diff; five of six pass SSIM; seed 47 is 0.82 dB below the PSNR threshold (mean_abs_diff 3.17, well inside). Visual inspection: the subject, shape and colors are preserved; differences are pixel-level. ### ti2i: 2D → 3D style conversion (A+B) Input is the shared CI edit image `TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg` (sha256 `0d56a63fca6ef8fe2a0ca27a0774c2bada9b2a198aeedbfdfb23bec09d0d3901`), prompt `Convert 2D style to 3D style`, seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1. End-to-end on one A3 chip (A+B, `quality="lossless"`): 23.1 s at 1024×1024 (denoise 16.69 s, 0.417 s/step, decode 2.79 s) and 36.8 s at 1536×1024 (denoise 28.25 s, 0.706 s/step, decode 4.74 s). ### multi-image editing (A+B) Two reference images (`edit2509_1.jpg` magician bear, `edit2509_2.jpg` alchemist bear, from the Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 test set), sent as two `image` fields to HTTP `/v1/images/edits`; seed 42, 40 steps, guidance 1, 1024×1024, `quality="lossless"`. The server log confirms the request carries both paths. - **Composition** — with the multi-image CI prompt ("The magician bear is on the left, the alchemist bear is on the right, facing each other in the central park square."), both identities are preserved (hat/robe/book/wand, graduation cap/cauldron/fan/Qwen shirt) and placed as instructed. - **Slot binding** — with "the bear from image 1 … image 2 …", uploading `[ref1, ref2]` puts ref1 on the left and ref2 on the right; uploading `[ref2, ref1]` swaps them. The second file lands in ``; it is not silently dropped or merged into the first. - **Ablation** — one reference at a time produces only that subject. - **Determinism** — repeating the request, or running it on a different chip, reproduces a byte-identical PNG. The CI case uses the two references staged for the NPU runner (the shared TI2I image and `rabbit.jpg`); the bear pair above is the manual slot-binding check. | request | CLIP | SSIM | PSNR (dB) | mean_abs | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | official (2 refs, CI prompt) | 0.9793 | 0.8285 | 17.78 | 10.182 | | order [1,2] | 0.9983 | 0.9631 | 26.58 | 1.972 | | order [2,1] | 0.9913 | 0.8986 | 21.39 | 5.811 | | ref 1 only | 0.9995 | 0.9947 | 39.80 | 0.666 | | ref 2 only | 0.9986 | 0.9768 | 25.97 | 1.992 | Differences vs eager concentrate on anti-aliased outlines and glyphs, with no structural or identity change (the amplified diff maps are edge-only). The edit case has no GT (`run_consistency_check=False`), so these numbers are supplementary evidence, not a consistency gate. ### Local recolor (A+B, CI case) Input is the shared TI2I image; the prompt changes the orange skirt and bow to deep blue, keeping the pose, face, hair, and SGL logo unchanged. ### RGBA / transparency (A+B) Prompt: an isolated cat on a transparent background, with `background="transparent"` and `output_format="png"`. | | alpha min/max | alpha mean | alpha<250 | alpha<128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | eager | 0 / 255 | 83.62 | 69.13% | 67.20% | | A+B | 0 / 255 | 83.70 | 69.11% | 67.17% | - alpha MAE 0.117, alpha max diff 32, transparent-mask IoU 0.9993 - RGB SSIM 0.9976, PSNR 46.70 dB The model does produce a meaningful alpha channel (~69% transparent pixels); A+B preserves it almost exactly. ### Manual check: transparent cat recolor with alpha (A+B) This is a separate manual check, not the CI recolor case above. Measurements are same-chip, same-seed pairs; a strict A,B,B,A ABBA round is reproducible with the commands above. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: enable the bit-exact Triton SiLU-mul fusion on HIP
issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's FFN activation fast path (fused_silu_mul_bitexact) is gated on current_platform.is_cuda(). On ROCm that predicate is False (PlatformEnum.ROCM), so the optimization is dead code on AMD hardware — even though the fused kernel is plain Triton (no CUDA JIT / PTX) and reproduces the eager silu(a) * b chain bit-exactly on HIP.

This is the same situation the XPU port fixed in #41940, which enabled the identical kernel via (x.is_cuda or x.is_xpu). This PR does the equivalent for ROCm/HIP.

issues.title: [diffusion] quantization: packed Q/K/V projection for convrot_int8's comfy_kitchen backend
issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's QwenImage21Attention projects Q/K/V from one activation with three separate [C, C] linears. convrot_int8 has two kernel backends:

  • the JIT / customkernel backend (CC 9.0 / 10.0 / 12.0 / 12.1), which #38040 already gives a fused single rotation + activation quantisation for q/k/v sharing one input;

  • the comfy_kitchen backend, which serves the GPUs the JIT ops do not build for (CC 8.x Ampere/Ada, CC 10.3) and has no equivalent: every attention block pays two redundant ConvRot activation quantisations and issues three narrow GEMMs.

On a GPU with no FP8/NVFP4 tensor cores -- A100 (CC 8.0), RTX 30/40-series -- the comfy_kitchen backend is not a fallback, it is the only INT8 path, so this gap is real there.

Modifications

  1. layers/quantization/convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py: the fused kernel apply ran inline moves to a module-level int8_linear(x, weight, weight_scale, group_size, bias=None, split_out_features=None), and apply becomes a thin adapter. This is a pure refactor: the op, its argument order and its numerics are unchanged, and there is now a single place for the row-split cap. split_out_features lets a packed caller judge the row-split heuristic on the per-projection width instead of the packed width.

  2. models/dits/qwen_image21.py: teach the existing bf16 packing to also cover convrot_int8. The three int8 [C, C] weights and the matching [C, 1] fp32 row scales are re-homed onto one [3C, C] / [3C, 1] storage each, and _project_qkv_packed_convrot_int8 projects all three through a single int8_linear call. A new BitExactFusionGate verifies the first call against the module forwards and falls back on any mismatch, so the packed path can only ever be used when it is bit-exact.

  3. test/unit/test_qwen_image21.py: four new unit tests -- storage sharing keeps values and shares one storage; the packing predicate requires the convrot_int8 method; the consecutive-slice view rejects gaps and separate storages; the packed int8_linear call is bit-exact against the separate per-projection calls at production shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Packed call is bit-exact against the separate calls (max_abs = 0.0); cat(quantize(W_i)) equals quantize(cat(W_i)) exactly. End-to-end on A100 GPU 0 (1024x1024, 40 steps, CFG 1, seed 42), the output PNG md5 is identical to the frozen INT8 baseline: 05288a62012b1353230d53c3297cb67c. The whole flow is inside the existing bit-exact gate, so an unexpected mismatch disables the fusion rather than changing the output.

Speed Tests and Profiling

A100 GPU 0 (CC 8.0, comfy_kitchen backend), Qwen-Image 2.1, 1024x1024 @ 40 steps, CFG 1:

arm | denoise | per step | output md5 -- | -- | -- | -- convrot_int8, unpacked QKV | 9.059 s | -- | 05288a62... convrot_int8, packed QKV (this PR) | 8.796 s | 0.220 s | 05288a62...

Kernel level (M=4114, C=4096, group_size=256): 1.263 ms -> 1.005 ms per attention block (-0.257 ms/block, -8.2 ms/step); the whole saving is the removed ConvRot work.

Scope: on JIT-capable GPUs (H100/H200/Blackwell) the equivalent fusion already exists via the customkernel backend, so this PR is a backend-parity change with no effect there.

  • Format your code according to the pre-commit guide.

  • Add unit tests.

  • Update documentation / docstrings as needed.

  • Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

issues.title: [Perf] [XPU] quantization: Run block-FP8 linears weight-only (W8A16) on Xe2
issues.body:
## Motivation

Block-FP8 checkpoints (128x128 weight scales, e.g. Qwen3-32B-FP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8) run their linears on XPU in two steps. First `per_token_group_quant_fp8` quantizes the activation. Then `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` calls `scaled_mm` (oneDNN).

At decode sizes that path streams the fp8 weight at only 175-350 GB/s on Arc Pro B70; the bf16 GEMM reaches 510-590 GB/s. So Qwen3-32B-FP8 decodes no faster than bf16, even though it reads half the bytes. Xe2 has no FP8 math, so fp8 activations buy nothing. The win is bandwidth: keep the activation in bf16 and stream the fp8 weight once.

## Dependency

The fused GEMM is `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20`, added in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#587. sglang currently pins sgl-kernel-xpu 0.5.0, which does not have it.

- This PR detects the op (`has_xpu_w8a16_gemm`). Without it, block-FP8 linears keep today's `scaled_mm` path unchanged, so this PR is safe to merge before the kernel release.
- The speedup arrives with the sgl-kernel-xpu version bump that includes #587.
- Until then, the fused-path unit test skips in CI and the dequant test runs.

## Modifications

- New `kernels/ops/gemm/fp8_w8a16_xpu.py`, with `xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear(input, weight, weight_scale, bias)`:
  - Up to 512 rows it calls `fp8_w8a16_mm_xe20`, which dequantizes in registers and streams the weight once.
  - Above 512 rows the GEMM is compute-bound. The weight is dequantized to bf16 by a small Triton kernel (one program per 128x128 scale block, edge blocks masked) and multiplied with `F.linear`. On these shapes that is faster than both `scaled_mm` and the fused kernel.
  - 512 is where the two paths tie at Qwen3-32B TP4 shapes on B70; the comment says so.
- `layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`: on XPU, `_dispatch_auto_backend` returns `xpu_w8a16_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` when the op exists. That function falls back to `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` when there is a static input scale, when the input is not bf16, or when the block size is not `[128, 128]`.
- New `test/registered/xpu/test_fp8_w8a16_linear_xpu.py`:
  - The dequant kernel must be bit-exact against a reference, including partial scale blocks (N=320, K=448).
  - Both paths (1, 24, 512 and 513 rows, with bias) must match the dequantized-weight reference.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K: sgl-eval, full 1319 questions, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8, thinking off, max 2048 tokens, seed 0.

| model | old FP8 path | this PR | bf16 checkpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-32B-FP8, TP4 | 94.84% | 95.22% | 94.31-94.77% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP2 | 95.00% | 94.77% | - |

`test_fp8_w8a16_linear_xpu.py`: 2 passed on Arc Pro B70.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:**
- Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, compute-runtime 26.31.
- The op from sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#587 was loaded as a torch library fragment on top of the released wheel.
- Server flags: cookbook BMG flags plus `--attention-backend intel_xpu --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`.

Per GEMM at decode (M=1, cold weights, in an XPU graph), Qwen3-32B TP4 shapes:

| GEMM | old `scaled_mm` path | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| qkv (N=2560, K=5120) | 49.7 us | 28.5 us (460 GB/s) |
| o_proj (N=5120, K=2048) | 38.4 | 21.7 (482 GB/s) |
| gate_up (N=12800, K=5120) | 222.6 | 119.2 (550 GB/s) |
| down (N=5120, K=6400) | 113.4 | 61.7 (531 GB/s) |
| per layer | 424 | 231 (1.84x) |

Prefill, one layer of 4 linears, in an XPU graph:

| rows | bf16 checkpoint | old `scaled_mm` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 547 us | 774 | 545 (fused) |
| 512 | 926 | 1943 | 1973 (fused) |
| 2048 | 3432 | 8295 | 4410 (dequant + bf16) |
| 4096 | 6783 | 16952 | 7975 (dequant + bf16) |

Prefill stays slower than the bf16 checkpoint, because the weight is still dequantized or streamed as fp8. It is much faster than the old path, though: c=16 TTFT for Qwen3-32B is 1049 ms, against 935 ms for bf16 and 1669 ms for the old FP8 path.

End to end, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 256 out:

| Qwen3-32B, TP4 | c=1 TPOT | c=4 | c=16 | c=32 | c=16 tok/s | c=32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 checkpoint | 31.57 ms | 32.48 | 34.97 | 40.28 | 415 | 715 |
| FP8, old path | 30.98 | 31.80 | 35.23 | 40.91 | 384 | 653 |
| FP8, this PR | **19.88** | 20.98 | 23.78 | 29.58 | **575** | **926** |

| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP2 (attention linears) | c=1 TPOT | c=4 | c=16 | c=32 | c=32 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old path | 8.95 ms | 13.65 | 22.70 | 29.82 | 1010 |
| this PR | **7.34** | 11.93 | 21.08 | 28.18 | 1070 |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 does not load at TP4: the per-rank MoE intermediate size, 768/4 = 192, is not a multiple of the 128 block. TP2 works.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
