issues.title: [Feat] diffusion/minimax-h3: Add an online FP8 video VAE decoder
issues.body:
## Motivation

The MiniMax-H3 video VAE decode is dominated by its 36 ViT decoder blocks: 144 FP16 linears (`attn.to_qkv`, `attn.to_out`, `ff.w1`, `ff.w2`) run over every tile of every window, and there is no quantized checkpoint for the VAE. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 the decode stage takes 3.26 s of a 30 s five-step 768p request.

This PR converts those 144 linears to W8A8 FP8 once at load behind `--component-quantizations.video_vae fp8`: per-output-channel weight scales, dynamic per-token activation scales and the shared `apply_fp8_linear` dispatch, the recipe the DiT's online `--quantization fp8` already uses. The decode stage drops by 40% at a worst-frame PSNR of 51 dB against the FP16 decoder. It is a lossy, deployment-level option outside the quality levels: opt-in by flag, it changes the output at every level including `exact`, and the docs say so.

Stacked on #45179: the base is `main`, so this PR also includes #45179 and its cleanup. Merge #45179 first to isolate the FP8 changes. The FP8 decoder runs on #45179's batched decode and output kernels.

## Modifications

Shared FP8 linear (`runtime/layers/quantization/online_fp8_linear.py`):

- `OnlineFP8Linear.from_linear` quantizes a prepared FP16/BF16 CUDA `nn.Linear` with `per_token_group_quant_fp8(weight, in_features)` (per-output-channel e4m3 weights, the online recipe of `Fp8LinearMethod`), keeps the bias and runs `apply_fp8_linear` with dynamic per-token activation scales (CUTLASS / tuned-Triton dispatch). `forward_quantized` takes rows a fused producer already quantized (`input_scale`, `pre_quant_output_dtype`). Inference-only; dtypes are pinned across `.to()`.

H3 install (`minimax_h3_video_vae/fp8.py`, `loader/component_loaders/vae_loader.py`, `models/vaes/minimax_h3.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/minimax_h3.py`):

- The flag reaches `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE.quantize_decoder_fp8` from the VAE loader before `optimize_vae`. `install_fp8_block_linears` validates the released 36-block / 144-linear scope (shapes and biases) before replacing anything, requires resident prepared FP16 weights, swaps the linears and decides once (`structure_reject_reason`) whether the blocks can run on the fused producers. Only those four linears per block change: the encoder, the patch embedding, the norms, the attention core (weightless Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE and SDPA) and the decoder output projection `proj_out` keep their precision. No other VAE accepts the option.
- Startup validation: `fp8` only; `--component-quantization-ignored-layers.video_vae` is rejected instead of silently ignored; CUDA SM100+, the FP16 decode autocast recipe (no `--component-precisions.video_vae`, no `--disable-autocast`) and a resident video VAE are required. The validated `quality: "high"` fingerprint gains `video_vae_quantization=None`, so a server started with the flag rejects `high` requests at admission.

Fused producers (JIT, SM100+; `kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/minimax_h3_vae_residual_norm.cuh`, `silu_mul_quant_fp8.cuh`):

- `minimax_h3_vae_residual_rmsnorm_fp8` (FP32 residual update + RMSNorm + dynamic per-token e4m3 quantization), `minimax_h3_vae_rmsnorm_fp8` for the decoder input, `minimax_h3_vae_residual_layernorm` (the last residual folded into the output LayerNorm) and `silu_mul_quant_fp8` under `kernels/ops/diffusion/quantization/` (`silu(gate) * up` quantized without the 16-bit round trip). The quantization epilogue follows `per_token_quant_fp8`.
- `fused_decoder.block_forward` feeds each block from these and reuses `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` for the weightless Q/K RMSNorm+RoPE. The producers run whenever the FP8 decoder is installed, at every quality level; per-call admission looks only at tensors (device, FP32 3-D input, rope table, no mask, no grad / compile / stream capture) and otherwise falls back to the eager FP8 path. The attention runs on the block's configured backend (`torch_sdpa` by default); it does not go through the cuDNN SDPA rebinding of the FP16 `lossless` path, so pass `--component-attention-backends video_vae=torch_cudnn_sdpa` to keep it on cuDNN.

Runtime weight updates and the decode-dtype store:

- `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE.validate_weight_update_source` rejects `/update_weights_from_disk` and `/update_weights_from_tensor` requests that include `video_vae` while the FP8 decoder is installed, before any weight is written: the updater's in-place copy would overwrite the e4m3 payload and leave the per-channel scales stale while reporting success. `WeightsUpdater` now runs the weight-update hooks on any module that defines them (previously `BaseDiT` only); without FP8 the VAE keeps taking updates.
- Applies to every MiniMax-H3 resident start, FP8 or not: `vae_loader._hold_decoder_weights_in_decode_dtype` writes and adopts the file-backed decode-dtype store only while the component's parameters live on the host. A store left by a host start (`--performance-mode auto` below 120 GiB) was otherwise adopted by a later resident start, which moved the CUDA FP16 decoder weights back to host mappings and failed the FP8 install; resident starts also no longer write an empty store.

Docs: cookbook section "Advanced: online FP8 video VAE decoder (deployment-level, lossy)" and the deployment-details bullet; the CLI reference rows for `--component-quantizations`; kernels README; `existing-fast-paths.md`; performance skill.

Tests:

- GPU (SM100+): `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_decoder.py`: `OnlineFP8Linear` against the dequantized math and `forward_quantized` against `forward` on pre-quantized rows; two real decoder blocks fused vs eager FP8 on `TORCH_SDPA` and `TORCH_CUDNN_SDPA` (relative RMS < 1%, cosine > 0.99995); the installer swaps exactly the 144 linears and keeps `proj_out` / `x_embedder` FP32, while runtime weight-update rejection is covered by the CPU tests below. `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_producers.py`: against an eager reference (`F.rms_norm` / `F.layer_norm` / `F.silu`, then the dynamic per-token e4m3 quantizer), scales within fp32 rounding (rtol 3e-6), >= 99.9% identical e4m3 bins and a half-ulp bound on the dequantized values (shared `discrete_flip_rate` helper); FP32 residual / LayerNorm outputs within atol 4e-6 / rtol 3e-5; inputs with fewer than two dimensions, mismatched residual shapes or an odd gate/up width are rejected before `view` could reinterpret them.
- CPU: `test_server_args.py` (fp8 only, ignored layers rejected, SM100 / FP16-autocast / resident requirements), `test_vae_loader.py` (only the H3 video VAE admits the override, quantized before `optimize_vae`; with a CUDA device of any SM, a host-start store does not pull the FP8 decoder to the host), `test_vae_decoder_store.py` (a resident start neither adopts nor writes a store), `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_weight_update.py` (tensor and disk updates rejected before any write, a decoder without FP8 keeps taking updates).

## Accuracy Tests

Not bit-identical by design. Setup as in #45179: 4x RTX PRO 5000 (SM120), TP2 + Ulysses2, t2va 768p 16:9 5 s, 5 steps, seed 1101, default `torch_sdpa` for the video VAE; the reference is `main` (62cee1b15c, the rebase base) at the same quality level, so the DiT trajectory is identical and only the VAE differs. ffmpeg PSNR / SSIM on the decoded frames, audio compared as a hash. Two or three runs per row produced identical outputs.

| Decoder | Request | worst frame PSNR | mean PSNR | SSIM min | Audio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FP8 | `lossless` (default) | 51.4 dB | 51.9 dB | 0.995 | identical |
| FP8 | `exact` | 51.3 dB | 51.8 dB | 0.995 | identical |
| FP16, #45179 | `lossless` | 52.1 dB | 52.6 dB | 0.995 | identical |

On this clip the FP8 decoder costs about 0.7 dB on top of the FP16 batched decode; the fused producers (both FP8 rows) and the tile batching (the `lossless` row) do not add to it. On fl2va (first-frame conditioning) the previous revision of this branch measured a worst frame of 44.0 dB, next to 44.2 dB for its FP16 decode against the same reference; that clip's VAE-only difference is larger for both decoders.

Runtime weight update, live 4x SM120 server: before the fix, updating `video_vae` with the checkpoint's own weights reported success and the next request decoded at 26.8 dB worst-frame PSNR (SSIM min 0.52) against the pre-update output; with it the request is rejected before any write and the frames are bit-identical. Decode-dtype store: a `--performance-mode auto` start followed by an FP8 resident start now loads and decodes in the same time as a store-disabled run (before, the loader aborted).

Tests on SM120: `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_decoder.py` + `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_producers.py` + `test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py` + `test_model_fast_paths.py -k "minimax_h3 or h3_vae or fp8_linear"`, 45 passed. The MiniMax-H3 and VAE unit files pass on CPU (387 cases, with a CUDA device visible for the two store cases). No CI case compares the FP8 decoder with the FP16 decoder's output yet; the fidelity numbers above come from the end-to-end runs. The kernel tests are registered on the `4-gpu-b200` lane, so this PR's CI is their first run on SM100.

Tests on B200 (SM100, torch 2.14.1+cu130) after the rebase onto `main` 2da6c0c237: `test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py` + `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_decoder.py` + `test_minimax_h3_vae_fp8_producers.py` + `test_model_fast_paths.py`, 136 passed, 21 skipped, 1 failed (`test_ernie_qknorm_rope_is_bit_exact`, which fails identically on `main` and on the PR base in that environment; see #45179). CPU: the MiniMax-H3 and VAE unit files plus `test_server_args.py`, 349 passed; the one failure is a `main` MOVA case that needs Hub access.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment and protocol as in #45179 (4x RTX PRO 5000 72 GB SM120 PCIe, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, sgl-kernel 0.4.9, flashinfer 0.7.1; TP2 + Ulysses2, t2va 768p 5 s, 5 steps, blocks interleaved, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`). Decode = `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` duration; peak = runtime peak reserved.

| Decoder | Request | decode ms, median (min–max) | vs `main` same level | vs FP16 #45179 same level | peak reserved |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16, `main` | `lossless` | 3258 (3252–3264), n=2 | | | 58120 MB |
| FP16, #45179 | `lossless` | 3158 (3147–3162), n=3 | −3.1% | | 58120 MB |
| FP8 | `lossless` | 1931 (1931–1937), n=3 | −40.7% | −38.9% | 56192 MB |
| FP16, `main` | `exact` | 3404 (3402–3406), n=3 | | | 58120 MB |
| FP16, #45179 | `exact` | 3400 (3391–3409), n=3 | within noise | | 58120 MB |
| FP8 | `exact` | 1998 (1989–2007), n=2 | −41.3% | −41.2% | 56190 MB |

Numbers are on the rebase base 62cee1b15c; `main`'s `exact` decode is slower than its `lossless` one there because #44690 dropped the Triton QK RMSNorm+RoPE the ViT attention ran at every level (see #45179). The `exact` row is the FP8 GEMMs plus the fused producers; `lossless` adds the tile batching (−3%). The previous revision gated the producers by quality level, and its `exact` row (FP8 GEMMs with the eager producers) measured 2098 (2096–2107) ms on 57db5089c2, so the producers are worth about 100 ms, or 5% of the FP8 decode time. End to end, the five-step `lossless` request moves from 30.2–30.3 s to 29.0 s (`exact`: 30.5–30.6 s to 29.2 s).

Kernel microbenchmarks (one SM120 GPU, width 2048 / FFN 8192, measured with a local script that is not part of this PR; `split` is the eager FP32 chain followed by `per_token_quant_fp8`):

| rows | op | split µs | fused µs |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1792 | residual_rmsnorm_fp8 | 45.5 | 20.3 |
| 1792 | residual_layernorm | 42.6 | 20.4 |
| 1792 | rmsnorm_fp8 | 21.9 | 14.2 |
| 1792 | silu_mul_quant_fp8 | 66.1 | 50.8 |
| 7168 | residual_rmsnorm_fp8 | 261.7 | 132.1 |
| 7168 | silu_mul_quant_fp8 | 489.3 | 244.6 |

Not measured on the other SM100+ hardware the option accepts (B200 / B300, GB200 / GB300, RTX 5090 and the other SM120 cards); Hopper is rejected at startup. No benchmark script ships with this PR.

issues.title: [Perf] sdar: Share block refresh with next-block denoising
issues.body:
## Motivation

SDAR runs a full-model KV refresh after completing each block. The next block then starts with a separate denoising forward.

This opt-in change shares those forwards at batch size one. Each layer refreshes the completed block before next-block attention reads its KV.
The gate/up projection uses both blocks together. QKV, attention-output, and FFN-down projections retain their original row counts on two ordered CUDA streams.

## Scope and behavior

- Dense SDAR, BF16 weights/KV, LowConfidence, FDFO, TP=PP=1, and native FlashInfer ragged attention.
- Enable `SGLANG_SDAR_REFRESH_PAIR=1`. The default is disabled.
- Keep the threshold, token selection, terminal refresh, and model weights unchanged.
- Use native execution for larger batches and unsupported request features. Discard pending predictions before incompatible batch changes or retraction.
- Validate configuration and capture the extra graph before readiness. Compare the first eligible live transition against native graph execution.
- Preserve normal profiler spans and GPU-time accounting. Reject unsupported memory-saving, offloading, debugging, and speculative modes.
- Reject online weight updates while enabled. The session guard checks every selected runner before changing weights.
- Disable sharing after native graph replacement and discard pending predictions before reuse.

The adapter borrows one scratch KV block per paired call and releases it afterward. Scratch slots never enter the scheduler request table.
There is one model weight copy. The extra graph and attention metadata consume additional memory.

[Usage and test commands](https://github.com/vishal1383/sglang/blob/7402129c76586f461a1a7aec58f0c7ea914190f1/benchmark/dllm/sdar_refresh_sharing.md).

## CPU and GB10 validation

- 163 CPU tests passed, including existing diffusion/FDFO and KV-location regressions.
- The registered original-B4 regression passed three additional full-output comparisons on this head's exact source, including repeated-request reuse. Total: 46 comparisons across the two validation runs.
- 43 exact-output comparisons passed: three registered B4, 16 initial B16/B32, and 24 paired timing comparisons. Another 24 main-branch SGLang timing requests matched their initial references.
- Both B16/B32 N1-to-N2 transitions passed: prediction discard, mask restoration, drain, and request-slot reuse.
- B16/B32 numerical qualification reported zero logit differences for both blocks.
- Repository-configured Ruff, isort, CI registration, and whitespace checks passed.

The numerical check requires finite logits, `atol=0.01`, `rtol=0.01`, equal greedy IDs, and equal confidence decisions.
Failure disables sharing and restores native execution. The first-transition check is not a proof of bitwise equality for all inputs.

## Performance

### A100: current PR source

One NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, BF16, concurrency 1, confidence threshold 0.95, FDFO, CUDA Graphs, and native FlashInfer 0.7.2.
Both variants disabled radix caching and scheduler overlap.
Each block size used eight retained ShareGPT prompts and two trials, with variant order reversed between trials.
Each cell used eight full-workload warmup requests before eight timed requests, with identical output caps and native EOS.

| Model / block size | Threshold | Main-branch SGLang mean request latency (ms) | Patched SGLang (ms) | Speedup | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SDAR-8B-Chat, B4 (original) | 0.95 | 4346.4 | 3701.6 | **1.174x** | **14.83%** |
| SDAR B16 | 0.95 | 2879.8 | 2734.8 | 1.053x | 5.03% |
| SDAR B32 | 0.95 | 2113.5 | 2076.8 | 1.018x | 1.74% |

These are warmed full-request latencies, including prefill, generation, scheduling, and HTTP.
For each block size, all 16 timed patched outputs and 16 patched warmup outputs matched the main-branch SGLang reference exactly.
The comparison checked output token IDs, text, and finish reasons.
Each patched server passed numerical qualification before timing. No qualification or fallback occurred during timing.
B4 trial speedups were 1.149x and 1.199x. Seven of eight B4 prompt means improved; the one-token response was 0.37% slower.

The A100 B4 and B32 qualification checks reported zero logit difference for the checked blocks.
B16 had a maximum absolute logit difference of 0.0625, within `atol=0.01, rtol=0.01`, with unchanged greedy IDs and confidence decisions.
These checks do not establish universal bitwise equality.
Device-memory samples increased by 158 MiB for B4, 230 MiB for B16, and 286 MiB for B32.
These nvidia-smi samples measure device memory use; the GB10 table below uses live PyTorch allocations.

Patched source: `7402129c76586f461a1a7aec58f0c7ea914190f1`.
Main-branch SGLang baseline: `773cb938fe9484a8f7e7e46fb1b1fe96412c59ed`.
The small cohort supports an initial comparison at N1 and threshold 0.95.

### GB10

One NVIDIA GB10 (Spark664c), BF16, N1, FDFO, CUDA Graphs, and native FlashInfer 0.7.2. Radix caching and overlap scheduling were disabled for both variants.
Each variant used four fixed ShareGPT prompts, repeated three times, with identical output caps and native EOS.
Memory reads ran outside timing. Transition instrumentation was installed after timing.

| Block | Threshold | Main-branch SGLang mean request latency (ms) | Paired (ms) | Speedup | Extra live PyTorch allocation (MiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B16 | 0.95 | 9388.9 | 8106.1 | 1.158x | 168.3 |
| B32 | 0.95 | 5411.8 | 5101.5 | 1.061x | 192.8 |

The first paired request includes numerical qualification. B32 first-request latency increased from 5857.7 ms to 5940.2 ms despite the warmed improvement.
Observed readiness times changed from 166.1 to 190.0 s for B16 and from 166.0 to 169.0 s for B32.
These observations include loading, compilation, and three-second polling. They do not isolate graph-capture cost.
Extra allocation uses PyTorch allocator snapshots; it excludes allocations outside PyTorch.

Main-branch SGLang source: `773cb938fe9484a8f7e7e46fb1b1fe96412c59ed`.
The timed source differs from this head only by the final two-line startup rejection of unsupported speculative decoding. Forward and replay code are identical.
The registered B4 regression was rerun on this head's exact source.

Checkpoint pins: B4 `ac4528d2c076b04e02a03e6f430efa4385331ce8`; B16 `f8a34a569baede49f65b1363548a5a0683fba3b5`; B32 `76fd4333a0c7e14a92e9873f05c295fd6954991a`.

<details>
<summary>Earlier measurements on the previous PR source</summary>

These results belong to `a06eaef95dfc8a47750511c67c5b8609e2540a42`, before the startup and lifecycle refinements.
They used the same GB10 hardware, precision, concurrency, and timing method.
These GB10 timings use the earlier source. Current-head A100 B4 results appear above.

| Block | Threshold | Main-branch SGLang mean request latency (ms) | Paired (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B4 (original) | 0.95 | 21803.8 | 16552.9 | 1.317x |
| B16 | 0.90 | 8409.4 | 7125.9 | 1.180x |
| B32 | 0.90 | 4829.1 | 4487.5 | 1.076x |

</details>

All reported speedups compare patched SDAR with main-branch SGLang SDAR at the same block size, threshold, precision, and concurrency.
Full-request latency includes prefill, generation, scheduling, and HTTP. The small sample does not establish a workload-wide gain.

## Related work and CI

[FDFO overlap scheduling #40756](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40756) targets scheduling overhead.
[Block-extend attention #39739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39739) targets attention decomposition.
This change shares work across a completed-block boundary.

The current [base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40166410395/job/121088329566) and [AMD](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40166410325/job/121088260400) gates stop because the required `run-ci` label is missing. The model tests did not run.
Authorized upstream CI and maintainer review are still required before merge.

issues.title: [Fix] spectrum: reset Spectrum state per CFG branch
issues.body: Fixes #35053. Spectrum now initializes each independent CFG branch at denoising step 0. Negative-only ranks therefore use the configured skip window and discard forecast history from previous requests. Under CFG parallel, ranks of the remaining shared-state models also reset their local state. `SpectrumParams.get_total_forward_steps` counts one local forward per step via a new keyword-only `cfg_parallel` flag (default `False`). No current model reaches this path (FLUX now has per-branch state, and MiniMax-H3 does not support CFG parallel); it keeps any shared-state model correct once it enables CFG parallel. Serial shared-state models keep positive-branch reset ownership, and the public full-reset API remains available. FLUX now gets per-branch Spectrum state, like Wan/Hunyuan/SD3. With serial true CFG, its cond and uncond forwards used to share one counter and one forecaster. As a result: - the forecaster mixed cond and uncond features; - CFG gating, which stops the uncond forward after the gate step, shifted the cond skip schedule; - the end-of-run wrap never fired. Embedded-guidance FLUX.1-dev runs a single branch and is unaffected. Cache algorithms, thresholds, and defaults are unchanged. Adapted the branch-local reset from @Oxygen56's unmerged PR #35140, with production-context regression tests using real tensor forecasts. The tests cover separate CFG ranks (Wan and FLUX), both serial branch orders, completed/interrupted requests with changed feature shapes, debug statistics, shared-state models, topology-aware forward counts, and FLUX under CFG gating (cond decisions and outputs match the ungated run). Supersedes #42157 (branch renamed to follow the repository's branch naming). ### Validation **Unit:** the new lifecycle tests, run against upstream `main`, `main` with both fixes, and both fixes with FLUX moved back to one shared Spectrum state: | Test | `main` | `main` + both fixes | both fixes, FLUX shares one Spectrum state | |---|---|---|---| | `test_cfg_ranks_initialize_the_same_skip_schedule` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_flux_cfg_gating_keeps_cond_schedule` | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | | `test_reused_model_matches_fresh_model_after_request_restart` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_serial_cfg_keeps_branch_forecasts_independent` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_shared_cfg_state_is_not_reset_twice` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `test_total_forward_steps_count_local_forwards` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | `test_shared_cfg_state_is_not_reset_twice` guards serial shared-state behaviour that `main` already had, so it passes everywhere. Together with the other fix on top of `main`, the Spectrum/TeaCache lifecycle tests, existing Spectrum forecaster, MiniMax-H3 Spectrum, CFG gating/policy, DiT config boundary and sampling-parameter tests give 77 passed and 59 subtests passed. Repository pre-commit hooks pass. **End to end** on B200 (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers, 832x480, seed 42, guidance 3.0, Torch SDPA; compile/BCG/warmup off), comparing upstream `main` with `main` + both fixes. FLUX runs use `yujiepan/FLUX.1-dev-tiny-random` (FLUX.1-dev architecture, random weights) with true CFG, so they compare behaviour, not image quality. *Request isolation:* a different-shape request runs first, then the target is compared with a fresh instance. | Model, topology | `main` | `main` + both fixes | |---|---|---| | Wan, 1 GPU serial CFG | bit-identical to fresh | bit-identical to fresh | | Wan, 2 GPU CFG parallel | negative rank fails `Spectrum feature shape must remain constant` (stale forecaster) → other rank hangs until timeout | bit-identical to fresh (frames and latents) | | FLUX, 1 GPU serial true CFG | same Spectrum decisions as fresh | same Spectrum decisions as fresh | | FLUX, 2 GPU CFG parallel | negative rank fails `size of tensor a (256) must match … (400)` (stale state) → other rank hangs until timeout | same Spectrum decisions as fresh | The tiny FLUX checkpoint is not bit-reproducible even without a cache: two fresh instances differ (max abs pixel diff 11), and so do repeated requests on one instance. This is run-to-run non-determinism, not state carried across requests, so FLUX isolation is judged by the absence of crashes and by identical per-step Spectrum decisions. *FLUX with CFG gating:* serial true CFG, 20 steps, gate at step 6. With per-branch state the cond decisions match the ungated run step for step; with FLUX on one shared state they do not. *Cost (Wan):* 33 frames, 30 steps, 3 prompts × 3 requests each. Spectrum skips 63% of DiT forwards in both topologies, with mean PSNR vs no cache 26.6 dB (1 GPU) and 27.2 dB (2 GPUs, CFG parallel), worst prompt 20.6 dB. Median speedup was 2.14× on 1 GPU; on 2 GPUs our shared nodes made timing noisy (median 1.33×, individual requests 2.5–5.1 s vs 4.8 s without a cache). Repeated requests on the same instance were bit-identical. The validation above was run locally and on our cluster. GPU CI needs the `run-ci` label from a maintainer. ### Update (2026-10-14) - **Merged current `main`.** Kept `force_spectrum_real` on `ForwardContext` while taking #43064's removal of the unused `attention_backend_cls`. The lifecycle test moved with the other diffusion unit tests to `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/` and, like them, drops per-file CI registration. - **CFG residual refresh uses real forwards.** When CFG gating refreshes its frozen cond-minus-uncond difference, both branches now run real forwards through the normal Spectrum hooks, so the difference never holds a forecast and both branch histories advance once. The forced-real scope is restored if a forward raises. On a small Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B CFG 5 regression (256x256, 17 frames, 20 steps, gate 0.3 plus Spectrum, two prompts), mean frame PSNR of the combined mode against the uncached run rose from 8.7 / 12.3 dB to 13.0 / 16.0 dB. - **Docs.** `spectrum.mdx` explains how Spectrum combines with CFG gating, measured on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B at its defaults: the combination is slower than Spectrum alone and no more accurate. - The FLUX.1 true-CFG Spectrum schedule and the per-model gating caps are in the follow-up #44261. Lifecycle and gating unit tests on the merged branch: 14 passed, 21 subtests passed. ### Re-verification (2026-10-15) On the current head: `test_spectrum_lifecycle.py` and `test_cfg_gating.py` 14 passed, 21 subtests passed, 0 skipped; `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (Rust hooks skipped: no `cargo` here, no Rust files touched). The Wan CFG-gating numbers in the docs come from a real Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B run at its defaults, not from mocks. ### Update (2026-10-15) Merged `main` again (73 commits, including the FLUX.3 and MOSS-Image models). One conflict, in `forward_context.py`: `main` added a TRT-LLM sequence-metadata cache field to `ForwardContext` next to the field this PR adds, so both are kept. Lifecycle and gating unit tests on the merged head: 14 passed, 21 subtests passed, 0 skipped. `pre-commit run --all-files` passes twice (Rust hooks skipped: no `cargo` here, no Rust files touched). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #40117666291](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40117666291) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #40117666188](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40117666188) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #40117666258](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40117666258)

issues.title: [Quant] Select FlashInfer b12x NVFP4 GEMM by default on SM120
issues.body:
## Motivation

On SM120 (RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000) `--fp4-gemm-backend auto` resolves to `flashinfer_cutlass`. FlashInfer's `mm_fp4` has a backend built for SM120/SM121, `b12x`, and its own `auto` picks it first there. SGLang never passes that name and no CLI value reaches it.

Cold-weight GEMM at M=9, one RTX 5090, eight weight copies rotated inside a CUDA graph, percent of 1.792 TB/s:

| shape | cutlass | b12x |
|---|---:|---:|
| gate_up N=34816 K=5120 | 63% | 89% |
| down N=5120 K=17408 | 52% | 78% |
| lm_head N=248320 K=5120 | 65% | 92% |

Output is bit-identical between the two backends on the same quantized inputs (M=1 and M=9, max abs diff 0).

#35739 made the same change on the diffusion side (`platforms/cuda.py` defaults to `auto` on sm_120).

## Modifications

- `fp4_utils.py`: add `Fp4GemmRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_B12X = "flashinfer_b12x"`. `initialize_fp4_gemm_config` selects it for compute capability 12.x when the backend is `auto`. SM100 (`flashinfer_cutedsl`) and SM80–90 (`marlin`) are unchanged. An explicit `--fp4-gemm-backend` overrides `auto`.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`: add `flashinfer_b12x` to `FP4_GEMM_RUNNER_BACKEND_CHOICES`.
- `arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`: `--fp4-gemm-backend` help now says `auto` picks `flashinfer_b12x` on SM120/SM121 and lists the choice.
- `flashinfer_autotune.py`: `should_run_flashinfer_autotune` enabled the FP4 term only for `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_cutedsl`. Once `auto` resolves to b12x, an NVFP4 model on SM120 would have lost the autotune pass it gets today. FlashInfer exposes `B12xFp4GemmRunner(TunableRunner)`, so b12x is tunable; it joins the gate.
- `fp4_utils.py`: add `is_flashinfer_b12x()` beside the other backend predicates, and list the `flashinfer_b12x` -> `b12x` remap in the `get_flashinfer_backend` docstring.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_fp4_gemm_backend_sm120.py`: pins the `auto` table for SM120, SM121, SM100, SM90, the explicit override, and the `b12x` API name, and pins the autotune gate for b12x, cutlass, and marlin. CPU-only; device probes are mocked. Reverting the one-line autotune change fails `test_b12x_keeps_the_fp4_autotune_pass` and passes the other nine, so the gate is covered rather than merely exercised.

No weight-path change: `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod` prepares `cutlass` and `b12x` weights identically (128x4 swizzled scales, no shuffle), and `get_flashinfer_backend()` already strips the `flashinfer_` prefix.

Capability major `== 12` rather than `is_sm120` because FlashInfer 0.6.18 enables b12x on SM121 as well. b12x requires CUDA 13; the pinned 0.6.18 wheel is cu13, so there is no SGLang-side check.

## Accuracy Tests

Same weights, draft, and prompts; `cutlass` vs `b12x`; one RTX 5090; image `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:616a3e97f45191af975896cfa644279096cb31bd408a071c2e99ca7209c3cafe` (FlashInfer 0.6.17; the same lines apply on current `main`). Target `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-model-path incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`, greedy, **thinking on**, 1200 tokens, two repeats each. Outputs hashed equal, so this is a kernel swap, not a quality claim.

| prompt | cutlass tok/s | b12x tok/s | output SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| prose | 149.5 | 171.5 | equal |
| math | 230.1 | 264.6 | equal |
| Rust code | 191.7 | 220.2 | equal |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency 1 --warmup-requests 1 --seed 7`, the shape in the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's 5090 cells:

| backend | output tok/s | mean TPOT | accept |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| flashinfer_cutlass | 173.0 | 4.95 ms | 4.47 |
| flashinfer_b12x | 196.2 | 4.31 ms | 4.25 |

Accept on random prompts varies by run, so the decode step was also measured directly: one streamed request, one chunk per verify step, greedy, **thinking off**, three fixed prompts, two repeats. cutlass 21.5 ms, b12x 18.8 ms per step on every prompt (prose 125.5 → 143.8 tok/s, code 259.6 → 297.7, math 279.8 → 321.1; tokens per step identical, outputs bit-identical). Torch profiler on the live server: NVFP4 GEMM per verify sub-step 2.09 → 1.52 ms, same 26 calls.

**FlashInfer autotune.** Before this PR, SM120 `auto` resolved to `flashinfer_cutlass`, so an NVFP4 model satisfied the FP4 term in `should_run_flashinfer_autotune`. Resolving to b12x would have dropped that term and silently ended the autotune pass on those GPUs, so b12x joins the gate. With the gate in place the tuner does run on SM120: `[AutoTuner]: Tuning fp4_gemm: 100%|##########| 4/4 [00:00<00:00, 62.40profile/s]`. Without it there is no autotuner line at all.

The pass makes no measurable difference to decode. One RTX 5090, identical server flags apart from `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`, `bench_serving` random 8192/1024, 10 prompts, concurrency 1, seed 7, two runs each (shown run 1 / run 2). Both arms generated 10240 output tokens, the requested cap, and both logged accept length 5.3505, so the two ran the same number of verify steps and duration is the whole comparison. The bench output records aggregates only, so this is not a claim that the text matched byte for byte.

| autotune | output tok/s | mean TPOT (ms) | median ITL (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| on | 263.96 / 263.63 | 3.120 / 3.126 | 2.100 / 2.101 |
| off | 263.30 / 262.96 | 3.128 / 3.128 | 2.102 / 2.103 |

Autotune is ahead in both runs, by 0.25%, against a 0.13% spread between two runs of the same arm; n=2 makes that a direction, not a result, and it is far too small to matter for decode. Server start time was 50 s for both arms in run 1 and 50 s against 40 s in run 2, sampled by a 10 s poll, so any autotune startup cost is at or below the resolution of that check. The gate line preserves the behavior SM120 had before this PR; it does not buy throughput. Both the accuracy and speed tables above were taken with `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` on both sides, so the autotune gate does not affect the cutlass versus b12x comparison.

Not measured: batch > 1, prefill-heavy shapes, RTX PRO 6000, SM121. Scripts and raw outputs: https://github.com/thomgardiner/sglang-sm120-nvfp4

issues.title: [Perf] [XPU] flux2: Bit-exact FLUX.2-klein op substitutions
issues.body:
## Motivation

On Intel XPU, FLUX.2-klein pays for copies and kernel choices the backend doesn't need:

- RMSNorm copies every strided Q/K head view of the packed QKV (Qwen3 text encoder) before the kernel;
- the dual-block SwiGLU reaches a fused kernel, but the wrong one for these shapes: #41940 enabled the Triton `_packed_silu_mul_kernel` on XPU, where `sgl_kernel.silu_and_mul` is **1.3-1.4x faster**;
- the single-block tail materializes the eager SwiGLU output, then copies it again into `cat([attn, mlp])` — and the single-block tensor is strided, which is exactly where the Triton kernel stops paying for itself.

This PR removes all three on XPU. Every change is bit-exact, so no quality gate is needed. CUDA/ROCm behaviour is unchanged.

**What the two block types actually see.** Probed on a live klein-4B 1-step run at 1024x1024, by wrapping `_flux2_swiglu` / `_flux2_cat_swiglu` from a `sitecustomize.py` (so it reaches the spawned GPU workers) and aggregating by shape:

| caller | shape | row stride | contiguous | calls/step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| double blocks, image stream | `[1, 4096, 18432]` | 18432 | yes | 5 |
| double blocks, text stream | `[1, 512, 18432]` | 18432 | yes | 5 |
| single blocks | `[1, 4608, 18432]` | **27648** | **no** | 20 |

So 20 of the 25 SwiGLU sites per step are **strided**, and they are the ones commit 3 serves. This is why the contiguity check in commit 2 is not a conservative limitation — it is the predicate that routes the single blocks into commit 3.

## Modifications

Three commits, each reviewable on its own:

1. **`RMSNorm.forward_xpu` reads packed-QKV head views in place.** It passes the strided 3-D view to `sgl_kernel::rmsnorm` instead of `reshape`-copying it. The output is bitwise identical, and it saves 72 copies per request.
2. **FLUX.2 SwiGLU goes through `can_use_fused_packed_silu_mul()`.** On XPU that routes contiguous inputs to `sgl_kernel.silu_and_mul`: bit-exact, **1.427x** over main's Triton kernel at the 4096-token shape and **1.304x** at the 512-token shape. Strided inputs are rejected by the predicate, because `sgl_kernel`'s packed kernel copies a strided input first; they are served by commit 3 instead, which beats both main and eager there.
   - The CUDA-graph capture guard asks `torch.get_device_module(x.device)` instead of `torch.cuda`, which raises off CUDA. It stays behind `can_fuse and not verified`.
   - `srt`'s `is_device_stream_capturing` is not used, because it returns False mid-capture on ROCm.
3. **The single-block eager SwiGLU writes straight into the `to_out` input.** `_flux2_cat_swiglu` allocates the `[attn | mlp]` buffer once and writes `silu(gate) * up` into its right half. The GEMM input is identical to the cat's. **This is the larger of the two optimizations: 14.24 ms of the 15.78 ms/step total**, because it fires on all 20 single blocks.
   - It returns `None`, keeping the cat, in these cases:
     - off XPU;
     - when the fused kernel applies;
     - under `torch.compile`;
     - on a dtype or shape mismatch.
   - For klein-4B at 1024x1024 the fused kernel never applies at a single block (the input is strided), so in practice this path is taken on every one of them.
   - FP8/NVFP4 paths are untouched.
   - `mlp_act_fn.forward` is bypassed on this path, so forward hooks on it (e.g. layerwise NVTX markers) don't fire.

New tests:
- `test/unit/xpu/layers/`:
  - `test_xpu_rmsnorm.py`: the head-view predicate (CPU, so it also runs in the H100 unit suite) and bit-exactness vs the contiguous path;
  - `test_xpu_packed_silu_mul.py`: bit-exactness vs eager;
  - `test_xpu_flux2_cat_swiglu.py`: bit-exactness vs the cat, and each fallback case.

  The H100 unit suite walks `test/unit/` recursively, where the XPU-only tests skip. `pr-test-xpu.yml` does not run them yet; wiring them in, as `pr-test-musa.yml` does for MUSA, is a follow-up PR.
- `test_model_fast_paths.py::test_flux2_cat_swiglu_is_xpu_only`: checks that CUDA and CPU keep the cat.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Intel Arc Pro B60, 1 card, torch 2.14.0+xpu, sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0, bf16. Both arms are this branch (`1e290129ea`) and its base (`dc81f17b90`) in the same env on the same card, minutes apart — all three commits are pure Python, so the arms are a `git checkout` apart with no rebuild. 50 timed reps after 10 warmup, `torch.xpu.synchronize()` either side, on the probed shapes above.

**Double blocks — contiguous, 5 calls/step each shape:**

| shape | eager | main (Triton) | this PR (`sgl_kernel`) | vs main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[1, 4096, 18432]` | 1.097 ms | 0.956 ms | **0.670 ms** | **1.427x** |
| `[1, 512, 18432]` | 0.134 ms | 0.090 ms | **0.069 ms** | **1.304x** |

**Single blocks — strided `[1, 4608, 18432]`, 20 calls/step.** Measured as the whole `to_out`-input preparation, which is the comparable unit: main does `swiglu -> torch.cat`, this PR fuses the mul into the cat buffer.

| path | time | vs eager |
|---|---|---|
| eager swiglu + cat | 2.467 ms | 1.000x |
| **main**: fused (Triton, strided) + cat | **2.512 ms** | **0.982x — slower than eager** |
| **this PR**: `_flux2_cat_swiglu` | **1.800 ms** | **1.371x** |

On the shape 20 of 25 sites see, main's Triton path is a **net loss** once the `cat` it forces is counted; this PR is **1.396x** faster than main there. In isolation that kernel does gain on strided input (1.011x at T=4096, 1.595x at T=512 vs eager), but the separate output buffer it writes has to be copied again by the `cat`, which erases it.

**Per step**, weighted by the probed call counts:

| | main | this PR | saving | saving % | % of the 485 ms step |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 double blocks (image + text) | 5.230 ms | 3.695 ms | 1.535 ms | 29.35 % | 0.32 % |
| 20 single blocks | 50.240 ms | 36.000 ms | 14.240 ms | 28.34 % | 2.94 % |
| **total** | **55.47 ms** | **39.70 ms** | **15.78 ms/step** | **28.43 %** | **3.25 %** |

Against a measured klein-4B denoise step of **485.0 ms** (`sglang serve --enable-torch-compile --component-residency dit=resident,text_encoder=layerwise-offload`, `bench_serving --dataset vbench --num-prompts 20 --num-inference-steps 4` at 1024x1024, 20/20, 2.4915 s mean latency, 10430 MB peak), that is **3.25 % of denoise**.

**Caveat:** the per-step figures are built from isolated microbenchmarks on synthetic tensors of the probed shapes. They predict ~500 ms/step for an end-to-end run on `dc81f17b90` against this branch's measured 485.0 ms/step; that end-to-end arm has not been run, so the 3.25 % is a projection, not a measured delta.

## Accuracy Tests

All three changes are bit-exact by construction and asserted with `torch.equal` in the new tests.

- **XPU**, Arc Pro B60, torch 2.13.0+xpu. The new layer tests were run one file per command, then as a directory: 3 + 2 + 3 passed, and 8 passed.
- **XPU bit-exactness at the real shapes**, torch 2.14.0+xpu: every fused result in the benchmark above compared `torch.equal`-identical to the eager reference — on both arms, at all three shapes (contiguous 4096 / 512, strided 4608), including `_flux2_cat_swiglu`'s full `[1, 4608, 12288]` `to_out` input against `cat([hs, silu(gate) * up])`.
- **CUDA**, A100-SXM4-40GB, torch 2.13.0+cu130. `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/{test_model_fast_paths,test_activation,test_sites,test_norm}.py` were run on this branch and on the base:

  | | base | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | test_model_fast_paths | 65 passed, 1 failed, 21 skipped | 66 passed, 1 failed, 21 skipped |
  | test_activation | 11 passed | 11 passed |
  | test_sites | 24 passed | 24 passed |
  | test_norm | 171 passed, 1 failed | 171 passed, 1 failed |

  The two failures are identical on the base, so they already exist on main:
  - `test_hunyuan_quality_qknorm_matches_rmsnorm`: CuTe-DSL NVVM compile error;
  - `test_cutedsl_norm_scale_shift_shapes[dtype1-shape0-layer-True]`: 4 of 353,894,400 elements out of tolerance.
- **CUDA-graph capture** (A100), run under a real `torch.cuda.graph` capture:
  - inside a capture, the guard keeps `_flux2_swiglu` eager and unverified, and the replay is bit-exact;
  - outside a capture, the fused kernel runs and is bit-exact;
  - a re-capture after that is bit-exact too.

issues.title: [Perf] SenseNova-U1: BSHD q/k/v, fused MLP gate_up + SiLU, RoPE table…
issues.body:
## Motivation

Part of #37742. At 2048x2048 the NEO-Unify denoise forward runs 42 layers x 2
CFG branches per step over 4096 image tokens, so per-layer bookkeeping that is
neither GEMM nor attention adds up. An 8-step `--profile-all-stages` trace on
main shows three sources of it:

- **Layout copies.** Generation q/k/v are built in `[B, H, S, D]` and then
  transposed back to `[B, S, H, D]` (with `.contiguous()`) right before the
  attention call, which consumes BSHD. The bit-exact fused RoPE kernel from
  #40374 also works in BSHD, so on the BHSD path each of its six calls per layer
  (q and k, three axes) transposes in and out of it as well.
- **Unfused MLP activation.** `act_fn(gate_proj(x)) * up_proj(x)` runs two GEMMs,
  a SiLU kernel and a separate multiply kernel.
- **RoPE tables rebuilt in every layer.** Each of the 42 layers recomputes the
  same temporal, height and width cos/sin tables from the same positions, about
  ten tiny kernels per table. Their GPU time is small, but the ~20k launches per
  8 steps are paid on the CPU, and the denoise loop has little CPU headroom.

All three can be removed without changing a single output bit.

## Modifications

In `runtime/models/sensenova_u1/neo_unify/modeling_qwen3.py`, plus a load-time
packing call in `runtime/models/sensenova_u1/loader.py`. The cookbook's Ascend
note said the fused MLP packs its weights on first use; it now says they are
packed once at load time.

**1. Build generation q/k/v directly in BSHD.**

- The q/k/v construction in `Qwen3Attention.forward_gen` moves into a new
  `_build_qkv_gen(hidden_states, indexes, bshd)`. With `bshd=True` the
  projections, the per-head RMSNorms, the 3-axis (t/h/w) RoPE and the head-dim
  concat all stay in `[B, S, H, D]`, and the `transpose(1, 2).contiguous()` of
  q, k and v before attention disappears.
- New `apply_rotary_pos_emb_bshd(q, k, cos, sin)`: the same
  `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact` kernel and the same eager fallback as
  `apply_rotary_pos_emb`, on BSHD inputs. Both layouts share one eligibility
  check (`_use_fused_rope`) and one kernel call (`_fused_rope_bshd`), so the
  two cannot drift apart. The eligibility conditions are #40374's, unchanged for
  the BHSD caller; they only gain the sequence dimension as a parameter.
- `forward_gen` decides the layout before building q/k/v. It keeps `[B, H, S, D]`
  for the three consumers that read that layout: the eager (dense-mask)
  fallback, the NPU BNSD flash cache, and the `Cache.update` path. Those paths
  are unchanged.

**2. One gate_up GEMM plus a fused SiLU that rounds like eager.**

- `Qwen3MLP` already packed gate/up into one weight for the NPU `npu_swiglu`
  path, re-pointing both `nn.Linear` weights at slices of the packed buffer so
  the weights are stored once and `state_dict()` is unchanged. That helper is
  generalized (`_pack_npu_gate_up_weights` -> `_packed_gate_up_weight`) and
  reused on CUDA: one GEMM produces `[*, 2 * I]`, then
  `silu_and_mul_with_activation_rounding` does the activation.
- That kernel variant is what keeps this bit-exact. Its `kRoundActivation` path
  rounds `silu(gate)` to bf16 before the multiply and rounds the product once,
  which are exactly the two rounding points of eager `F.silu(gate) * up`. The
  plain `silu_and_mul` keeps the product in fp32 and would change the output.
- The CUDA path is taken in inference mode only (no grad, eval, bf16, `silu`,
  `intermediate_size % 16 == 0`, not under `torch.compile`); everything else
  falls through to the original code.
- Packing happens once, at load time: after `model.to(device)` the loader calls
  `Qwen3MLP.pack_gate_up_weight()` on every MLP and then empties the allocator
  cache. Packing lazily in the first forward instead left every freed 96 MiB
  gate/up pair reserved, since two of them cannot hold the next 192 MiB packed
  buffer: +13.8 GB peak reserved memory on H200 (36378 -> 50228 MB) with the
  same allocated memory.
- The packed weight is a view of the storage the two parameters share, not a
  cached tensor. Sleep mode (`release_memory_occupation`) moves parameters and
  buffers only, so a cached reference would keep ~13.5 GiB per GPU alive while
  asleep. Weights rebound to new storage (wake-up, weight update) are repacked
  on their next forward, which also empties the allocator cache for the same
  fragmentation reason; that happens once per MLP after such an event.

**3. Build the RoPE tables once per forward.**

- Every layer's `rotary_emb` / `rotary_emb_hw` is built from the same config,
  so their tables depend only on the positions and the dtype.
  `Qwen3Model.forward` builds the three `(cos, sin)` pairs once, after `indexes`
  is final (the single-token decode path rebuilds it inside the forward), and
  passes them down as `rope_tables`. The existing `**kwargs` plumbing carries
  them through the decoder layer; only `Qwen3Attention.forward_und` /
  `forward_gen` name the parameter.
- `Qwen3Attention.build_rope_tables` returns the shared tables when their dtype
  matches the layer's input and rebuilds otherwise. The tables are cast to the
  activation dtype, and a layer's input can differ from the embedding dtype
  (fp32 norm weights promote a bf16 input), so reusing them blindly would change
  the RoPE rounding. Called without tables (direct callers, tests), it behaves
  as before.
- This is the step before #40374's: that PR fused *applying* the tables
  (`q * cos + rotate_half(q) * sin`) into one kernel; this one stops
  *recomputing* them in every layer. The two compose.

## Accuracy Tests

The output is **bit-identical** to main, not merely close: 12 runs (4 main, 4
this PR, 4 this PR with per-layer RoPE tables) on H200 at 2048x2048 / 50 steps /
guidance 4.0 / seed 42 all produce a PNG with md5
`b95d2e9f57b48dc4e91fa20de8deca74`. Items 1 and 2 were also checked with the FA3
attention change from the follow-up PR stacked underneath (both builds give
`ca5f3dc015ac07a3b31a46cc822a3e42`).

The paths the default command does not reach are byte-identical to main as well:

| Path | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1024x1024 | cookbook command at 1024x1024, 8 runs (4 main, 4 PR) | one md5, `c7017ed1` |
| Dynamic batching (cookbook 5.1) | `--batching-max-size 2 --batching-delay-ms 100`, two concurrent requests with different prompts and seeds, 1024x1024 / 20 steps, 2 rounds | both images identical to main; the two responses finish within 1 ms of each other, so they ran as one B=2 batch (per-sample KV compaction, batched RoPE tables) |
| `think_mode=True` | Python API, 1024x1024 / 20 steps (exercises the single-token decode path, where `indexes` is rebuilt inside the forward) | identical to main, `92f43736` |

Not run on Ascend NPU. The NPU paths keep the `[B, H, S, D]` layout, but the
`npu_swiglu` MLP now uses the load-time packed weight.

Unit tests, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sensenova_u1.py`:
84 passed on H200; 81 passed, 3 skipped (CUDA-only) on CPU. Three cases are new:

- `test_sensenova_u1_gen_qkv_bshd_matches_bhsd`: the BSHD q/k/v build equals the
  BHSD build exactly. On CPU and on CUDA, where 128 tokens with 128-dim heads put
  the t/h/w RoPE on the fused kernel.
- `test_sensenova_u1_cuda_fused_mlp_keeps_eager_rounding`: the fused MLP output
  equals eager `down_proj(silu(gate) * up)` bit for bit.
- `test_sensenova_u1_shared_rope_tables_match_per_layer`: a 2-layer model through
  prefill, single-token decode and denoise matches the per-layer-table build
  exactly, and builds each table once per forward. Its denoise step feeds bf16
  embeddings to fp32 weights, so the dtype rebuild is exercised.

Each was checked to fail on a mutated build: swapping in plain `silu_and_mul`;
swapping `cos`/`sin` in the BSHD kernel call; and, for the RoPE tables, dropping
the dtype check, never reusing the shared tables, or building them before the
decode path rebuilds `indexes`. The existing NPU fused-MLP
test also asserts that the module holds no tensor outside its parameters and
buffers (a cached packed tensor would survive sleep mode).

Memory, 1x H200, cookbook command, `Max peak` reserved: main `bab9c81fea`
36542 MB, this PR 36446 MB (the first version, which packed lazily, measured
50228 MB).

Sleep mode on a 2-GPU server (with the CFG-parallel PR), `nvidia-smi` per GPU:
38.8 GB awake, 4.8 GB after `release_memory_occupation`, 38.6 GB after
`resume_memory_occupation`, 38.9 GB after the first request following wake-up,
which repacks every MLP (54.8 GB when the repack did not empty the cache). The
image is unchanged across the cycle.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment: 1x H200 (driver 595.71.05), Xeon Platinum 8558, torch
2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1; main `bab9c81fea`; local copy of
`sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT`. GPU clocks were logged during the profiles:
1.87 GHz mean SM clock under load, power-cap throttling only.

1x H200, local checkpoint, the cookbook single-GPU command
(`docs/cookbook/diffusion/SenseNova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT.mdx` §3.1),
`--warmup-mode request`, reading the `(with warmup excluded)` line, runs
interleaved on one GPU. The middle row is this PR with item 3 disabled (each
layer builds its own tables), to separate its effect:

```bash
sglang generate --model-path <SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT> \
```

issues.title: [Intel GPU] Add opt-in decode graph capture widths for DSV4 on XPU
issues.body:
## Motivation

- The DSV4 indexer sizes its paged gather and logits buffer from `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE`. On `intel_dev` that is the full configured context. At `--context-length 262144 --page-size 256` it is 262148, because the pool adds padding (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:558`).
- Graph capture freezes that width. So a short conversation does full-context indexer work on every decode step.
- CUDA has the same cost: #40441 measured 2.68x faster per-request decode at `--context-length 131072` than at 1048576 (8x H200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark).

## Modifications

- **Opt-in widths, XPU only.** `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS` (default empty, so off) lists narrower capture widths. On a device other than XPU, a non-empty value raises an error (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:509`).
- **One graph per width.** The backend advertises the widths and always appends the full context as the last width. The runner captures one graph per width and replays the smallest width that fits the batch. The graph key carries the width. The shared runner code names no backend.
- **Bad combinations fail at startup.** `validate_deepseek_v4_decode_graph_widths` (`deepseek_v4_hook.py:198`) rejects the variable together with any of these:
  - speculative decoding (`speculative_algorithm`)
  - diffusion decoding (`dllm_algorithm`)
  - two-batch overlap (`enable_two_batch_overlap`)
  - PDMux (`enable_pdmux`)
  - a decode graph backend other than `full`
- **Eager forward passes use the full context.** A narrowed width belongs to a graph replay only. Since 2340f8c401, eager decode metadata uses the full context (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:1465`). At 3c0dbe0052, it could use the width of the last replay. Then a long eager batch would lose its trailing pages.
- **Off means unchanged.** With the variable unset, the runner captures one graph per batch size, with the same graph keys as before. `AttentionBackend` and `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` carry class-level `None` defaults. So the draft runners that skip `super().__init__()` still work.
- **The XPU gate stays.** I did not measure this code on CUDA. I think a device-neutral version belongs on `main`, based on #38993.

## Accuracy Tests

| file | result at 2340f8c401 (CPU) |
| --- | --- |
| `test_decode_cuda_graph_widths.py` (new) | 27 passed |
| `test_decode_cuda_graph_widths_spec_runners.py` (new) | 9 passed |
| `test_deepseek_v4.py` (adapted) | 10 passed, 8 skipped (need CUDA). The run uses an `sgl_kernel` import stub. This CPU host needs the stub at the base commit too. |

- The tests cover:
  - the width resolver, and width selection at the boundaries
  - the unchanged path with the variable unset
  - the full-context bound of eager decode
  - the graph keys, the validator and the draft runners
- The eager-path regression test fails at 3c0dbe0052 (`8192 != 262148`) and passes now.
- No accuracy run checked this PR. I expect no change in model output. The widths change how much the indexer scans, and the last width is always the full context.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x Arc Pro B70, TP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, context length 262144. In each table, the width setting is the only difference between the rows.

**This PR's code (first revision), 1024 in / 1024 out, 1 user, 3 runs per row:**

| widths | tok/s per user | inter-token latency (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | 40.71 | 24.57 |
| `8192,32768` | 46.57 (+14.4%) | 21.47 (-12.6%) |

**A newer local build (2026-10-12), not this PR's code.** The build has local XPU changes that are not upstream yet. Two of them matter here:
- an earlier local version of this feature, which sets the same widths through another variable
- an indexer early exit: the indexer logits kernel stops at the length of each sequence, not at the longest sequence of the batch

Each figure is the mean of 2 launches:

| widths | 1k/1k, 1 user (tok/s per user) | 8k/512, 8 users (tok/s per user) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | 62.20 | 27.03 |
| `8192,32768` | 65.86 (+5.9%) | 28.66 (+6.1%) |

Each added graph costs about 0.42 s of capture time. Each added width keeps about 5 MB of device memory per rank. `max_total_num_tokens` changed by no more than one page (256 tokens) of jitter.

## Limits

- I found the eager-path defect by reading the code. No device run checked the fix.
- I measured this PR's code at 1024 in / 1024 out only. The gain should shrink as prompts grow toward the full context.
- I want a second opinion on one point. `can_run_graph` builds its graph key with the width label of the previous replay (`decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:526`). I found no wrong replay, because capture records every batch size x width combination.
- CI does not run on this PR, for three reasons:
  - The PR has no `run-ci` label.
  - The XPU lane runs only for pull requests to `main`.
  - The maintenance gate (#21065) blocks `intel_dev`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The feature is an environment variable with no doc page yet.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

issues.title: [cake_kernels] opt-in P1/P2 model routes: DeepSeek-V3 grouped routing, DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA decode, Mamba2 SSD/SSU, SP all-gather matmul, MiniMax-H3 diffusion stages (SGLANG_CAKE_ROUTES)
issues.body:
## Motivation
Part 2 of the Cake-kernel forwarding work for sgl-project/sglang#42176: opt-in wiring of the forwarded P1/P2 Cake kernels
behind `SGLANG_CAKE_ROUTES` (introduced in #42406). Nothing changes when the switch is unset; every route admits on the
real tensors at the call site and falls back to the stock kernel with identical arguments otherwise.

> **Stacked on #42407 (`cake/09-kimi-k3-e2e`) → #42406 and on the Part 1 groups #42384, #42385, #42386 (merged into this branch).** Review only this PR's own commits (the P1/P2 route commits and the FlashInfer-main re-validation commits on top).

## Routes added (`python/sglang/kernels/cake_kernels/_routes.py`)
| route | model family | engine call site | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsv3_grouped_routing` | DeepSeek-V3 / R1 / V3.2 | `srt/layers/moe/topk.py::biased_grouped_topk_gpu` | same positional contract as the stock FlashInfer branch; shared-expert append unchanged; FlashInfer host rejections cached per shape |
| `dsv4_sparse_mla_decode` | DeepSeek-V4 (trtllm backend, SM100/103), DeepSeek-V4.1 (SM120/121 default backend) | `deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py` decode / verify / varlen prefill; `deepseek_v4_backend.py` DSv4.1 mixed-cache decode | workspace-size admission, counter priming before CUDA-graph capture, grow-only split scratch (eager only); `dsv4/cake_routes.py` |
| `mamba_ssd_prefill`, `mamba_ssu` | Nemotron-H, granite hybrids (Mamba2) | `attention/mamba/mamba.py` SSD prefill and both `selective_state_update` sites via `mamba/cake_routes.py`; chunk-128 metadata built once per forward in `mamba2_metadata.py` | BF16/FP16 state, 128-multiple prefill; radix-cache track rows mapped onto the kernel's per-sequence checkpoints (`Mamba2Metadata.prepare_mixed`, chunk-aligned rows keep the engine's slot copy); calls in which every sequence is a single chunk-128 keep the stock kernel (see below); promoted SSU rows only |
| `sp_all_gather_matmul` | Llama-3.1-70B (`--enable-layernorm-sp`) | `srt/layers/layernorm_sp.py::column_parallel_g_matmul` | prepared / functional all-gather+matmul for unquantized BF16 participants; cached K-major weight copy; `LlamaForCausalLM` accepted as an SP architecture only while this route is selected. The FlashInfer kernel requires torch's **NVSHMEM** symmetric-memory backend: the route selects it in `distributed/bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime` (before the first symmetric allocation), the adapter admission checks it, a FlashInfer `ValueError` is a cached refusal, and torch's fused symm-mem SP ops are disabled for the process once NVSHMEM is selected (they cannot allocate under that backend). `SGLANG_CAKE_SP_CHECK=1` recomputes the stock all-gather + matmul per call and compares at BF16 tolerance (diagnostic) |
| `minimax_h3_diffusion` | MiniMax-H3 DiT (`multimodal_gen`) | `dits/minimax_h3.py` block stages via `minimax_h3_cake_routes.py` | per-stage admission (bf16 pre-attention pack, dense varlen attention, out-proj + gated residual, fc1 SwiGLU); GEMM stages only after an eager warm-up launch. Measured on MiniMax-H3 FL2VA t2va (1× GB200, 768p / 4 s / 8 steps): the attention stage is admitted on all 352 DiT calls, the GEMM stages on none (the engine's AdaLN tables have 6 or 3 rows, the FlashInfer stages require 9); e2e time unchanged (19.9 s vs 19.9 s), +0.9 GB peak; the Cake attention matches FlashAttention-4 within BF16 tolerance on the real shapes but is not faster, so the route stays opt-in |
| `dsa_indexer`, `msa_nvfp4_sparse_decode` | DeepSeek-V3.2 indexer, MiniMax-M3 | registered, **not wired** | engine contract mismatch (paged FP8 indexer logits / exact-shape dense-MQA plans; no NVFP4 KV pool for the MiniMax sparse path) — stock paths untouched |

Route logging: the first "taken" and the first fallback of every distinct reason are logged once per route
(`[cake-route] <route>: …`), so an e2e run can prove which kernel executed and why a batch did not take Cake.

## Tests
- New CPU unit tests (mocked adapters/forwarders; route off → stock with the exact kwargs; on + admitted → Cake with the
  contract arguments; rejected / inside capture / FlashInfer host rejection → stock, logged once):
  `test_cake_deepseek_routes.py` (21), `test_cake_mamba_sp_routes.py` (26), `test_cake_minimax_routes.py` (17).
- Gate on this branch head: ruff check/format, isort, codespell, whitespace clean; 68 new + 189 existing kernel-namespace
  tests pass.

## Model e2e (this round)
- **Nemotron-H-8B-Reasoning-128K BF16, TP1, 1× GB200**, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` in every arm.
  - Default server configuration: baseline vs `mamba_ssu,mamba_ssd_prefill` vs `mamba_ssd_prefill` → GSM8K-200
    0.890 / 0.895 / 0.895, decode 335.6 / 2454 / 7540 tok/s (bs 1/8/32) in every arm, bitwise-identical logprobs.
    **The Cake kernels did not run**: plain-decode SSU (T=1, headdim 64) has no promoted Cake row, and the SSD prefill
    route is rejected because the engine requests Mamba radix-cache track states on every prefill (not mapped onto the
    Cake checkpoint contract).
  - `--disable-radix-cache` in both arms (the SSD route admits 128-multiple prefills): GSM8K-200 0.890 → 0.885 / 0.900;
    single 1024-token request prefill **24.0k → 27.7k input tok/s, TTFT 42.6 → 37.0 ms**; bs 8/32 prefill within
    1.4 %; decode identical (SSU stock); serving (200 × 1024/128, conc 32) 36.4k → 37.0k tok/s with TTFT medians
    404 → 354 ms (serving TTFT is noise-dominated at this size: identical-kernel arms spread 277–408 ms). Greedy texts
    identical; a 1024-token input-logprob probe shows the kernel difference (mean |Δ| 0.035). Route log:
    `[cake-route] mamba_ssd_prefill: Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 1024, 128, 64)/bfloat16 …)`.
  - Kernel-level A/B at the model shape (stock Triton SSD vs the Cake route helper, random inputs, BF16 state): Cake is
    1.5–2.0× faster (0.25 vs 0.50 ms at 1024 tokens) and not bitwise: max |Δ| one bf16 ulp at |out| ≈ 90, mean |Δ| 0.0077;
    against an fp32 recurrent reference 1.5 % of outputs fall outside atol/rtol 1e-2 vs 0.6 % for the stock kernel (tracked
    internally; the route stays opt-in).
  - **Radix cache ON (follow-up commits in this PR)**: the engine's Mamba track-state requests are now mapped onto the Cake
    checkpoint contract, so the SSD route admits tracked 128-multiple prefills with the default server configuration
    (route log `Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 1024, 128, 64)…)`; GSM8K 200/50/50 q baseline 0.875/0.880/0.840 vs route
    0.895/0.900/0.860; fixed-prompt logprobs identical). A prefix-hit probe (1024 cached tokens + a 128-token extend) then
    returned all-NaN logits on the route arm; isolated at the kernel level to any call in which every sequence is exactly
    one chunk-128 (random *and* zero initial states, NaN count varies per call; batches with a ≥ 2-chunk sequence are
    clean). The route keeps the stock kernel for that geometry (host extend lengths; logged once) and the probe is clean
    again (same greedy ids as the cold run, max |Δlp| 0.0009 on the outputs); the kernel defect is tracked separately.
- **DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8, TP4, 4× GB200** (`--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, FlashInfer mHC kernels in both arms):
  baseline GSM8K 0.970 vs `dsv4_sparse_mla_decode` **0.020** — an e2e correctness regression. The route was taken on the
  SWA-only, c4 and c128 layers and on the varlen-prefill site; the eager (`--disable-cuda-graph`) arm scores the same, so
  it is not a capture/replay issue. An env-gated in-engine A/B (`SGLANG_CAKE_DEBUG_DSV4_AB`, this PR) re-runs the stock
  kernel on the identical tensors: returning the stock output restores GSM8K 0.980 with logprobs identical to the
  baseline, while the Cake output differs by up to 12–17 (abs) with 12–79 % of elements outside the FP8 tolerance. A
  standalone repro shows the upstream Cake SM100 kernel attends every column up to `sparse_topk` regardless of
  `sparse_topk_lens` (a poisoned tail beyond `lens` leaves the stock output bit-identical and destroys the Cake output)
  and does not apply the `seq_lens` sliding-window validity; FlashInfer's own hardening suite passes at the pin. Tracked
  upstream; **the route stays opt-in and must not be enabled until the FlashInfer fix lands.** Graph-batch rows also fall
  back on the compressed layers (workspace 1.1 GB > the 128 MiB engine buffer).
- **DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4, TP4, 4× GB200**: `dsv3_grouped_routing` is unreachable on this checkpoint — the
  `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner fuses the router (`BypassedTopKOutput`), so both arms ran identical kernels (GSM8K 0.970,
  bitwise-identical logprobs).
- **DeepSeek-V3-0324 FP8, TP4, 4× GB300** (real weights): under the engine default (`--moe-runner-backend auto` resolves
  to `flashinfer_trtllm` for DeepSeek-V3 fp8 on sm100) the route is likewise unreachable (0 route lines, arms bitwise
  identical, GSM8K-400 0.940 vs 0.938). With `--moe-runner-backend triton` in both arms the route is taken on every rank:
  GSM8K-400 0.935 → 0.945, every e2e metric within ±1 % (the router is microseconds per layer), memory equal. The arms are
  not bitwise identical (1024-token input logprobs: mean |Δ| 0.15 nat); a per-call stock-vs-Cake check inside the route
  (`SGLANG_CAKE_DSV3_ROUTING_CHECK=1`, eager) over 1.0 M routed rows per rank shows identical expert ids and order in
  every row and weights within one FP32 ulp of the stock FlashInfer router, while two identical stock servers are bitwise
  equal — the drift is the chaotic amplification of that rounding through 61 MoE layers, not a kernel defect. Perf-neutral,
  no production path uses it on sm100/sm103 while the default runner fuses routing; the route stays opt-in.
- MiniMax-H3: one e2e A/B on 1× GB200 (above); no video-quality eval in this round — frames differ from the stock run by
  ≈26 dB PSNR against a 36.8 dB stock run-to-run baseline, consistent with trajectory divergence from bf16 rounding-order
  differences (kernel outputs within tolerance), not certified quality-neutral.
- Llama-3.1-70B SP: GPU run on the real architecture with seeded dummy weights (1 node × 4 GB300, TP4, `--load-format dummy`,
  stock no-SP baseline vs the route): the prepared packed-QKV launcher is admitted for qkv (inp 2048×8192 bf16, weight 2560×8192,
  world 4), the per-call Cake-vs-stock check is bit-identical (1151 calls per rank, 19.7 G elements, max abs diff 0), and the
  arms' greedy tokens / logprobs are identical (256/256 tokens, 1023 input logprobs, max diff 0). e2e perf is **not** positive
  in this configuration: selecting the route forces the NVSHMEM symmetric-memory backend, under which sglang's custom
  all-reduce cannot allocate and falls back to NCCL (steady decode throughput ×0.77–0.80 at bs 1/8/32), and the prepared
  launcher is refused inside prefill CUDA-graph capture, so captured prefills run the stock SP path (TTFT ×0.99–1.02). Model
  quality on the real BF16 weights is not measured (checkpoint not reachable from the cluster). Keep the route opt-in.
- MiniMax-M2/M3: wiring + CPU tests only; MiniMax-M2 needs an NVFP4 checkpoint (none public: the warp-decode runner is
  NVFP4-only) and MiniMax-M3's MSA route needs an NVFP4 KV pool the engine does not have.

## FlashInfer main re-validation (`58171ea83f32185a7990cfc15c969ecf79bb406c`)
The Mamba2 SSD / SSU, SP all-gather+matmul and MiniMax-H3 contracts changed on FlashInfer main (any-seqlen exact-scan SSD
with token-major output and FP32 state, promoted headdim-64 SSU row, all-gather+matmul on the engine's `[N, K]` weight view
with any row count, MiniMax-H3 stages on the engine's native operands). The top commits move the three routes to those
contracts; the stock paths are untouched and the adapters keep every admission check the new kernels require. Re-measured
with FlashInfer main in the same container:

- **Nemotron-H-8B BF16 TP1, 1× GB200, radix cache ON, GSM8K-200 0.885 in all arms.** The SSD route now runs on every
  prefill of ≥ 128 tokens (log `Cake kernel selected (x=(1, 795, 128, 64) …)`); packed batches shorter than 128 tokens stay
  on the stock kernel (the FlashInfer host builds a fixed 128-row TMA token box and rejects shorter inputs — logged fallback,
  tracked upstream). `mamba_ssd_prefill`: bs1 prefill 22.5k → **28.9k input tok/s (TTFT 45.5 → 35.5 ms)**, bs32 prefill
  80.7k → 88.3k, decode unchanged, serving 36.3k → 38.1k tok/s. `mamba_ssu,mamba_ssd_prefill`: bs32 decode 7589 → **8380
  tok/s**, serving **40.1k tok/s**, TPOT 4.27 → 4.21 ms. Prefix-hit probes (1024+128, 1536+256): same greedy ids, no NaN.
  Kernel-level A/B at the model shape (random inputs, 128…1152 tokens, with/without initial states): Cake 0.12–0.15 ms vs
  stock Triton 0.42–0.55 ms (3.3–3.8×); against an fp32 recurrent reference 0.58–0.75 % of outputs fall outside atol/rtol
  1e-2 vs 0.55–0.70 % for the stock kernel (same accuracy class); the FP32-state Cake path gives bit-identical outputs to the
  BF16-state path, so the engine-default `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32` no longer silently receives BF16 states.

issues.title: [quant] compressed-tensors: honor .linear-wrapped ignore entries on fused shards
issues.body:
Fixes #28018.

The reported llm-compressor checkpoint spells its vision-tower `ignore` entries against the `CompressedLinear` wrapper (`...q_proj.linear`). For fused `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj`, SGLang expands the layer into shard names without that suffix, so `should_ignore_layer` misses those wrapped entries and quantizes the corresponding fused projections. That is 135 of its 189 wrapped entries; the other 54 name `o_proj` / `down_proj`, which `ClippableRowParallelLinear` already nests at `.linear`, so those already match.

The change is therefore on the fused path only: retry the wrapper spelling once per expanded shard, after the existing comparator misses. Four lines, no new matching primitive; #32736's no-prefix invariant is untouched.

Verified on one H200 with `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct`:

- **before** — the load reaches `compressed_tensors_wNa16` → `gptq_marlin_repack` and aborts with `size_n = 8608 is not divisible by tile_n_size = 64`, the message in #28018;
- **after** — the model loads, all 108 vision-tower projections come up `UnquantizedLinearMethod`/bf16, and `language_model.layers.0` stays `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod`;
- **minimal** — a third arm that also retried on the unfused path produced a byte-identical result.

Two behavior changes, your call:

- naming **only some** fused shards in the wrapped spelling previously loaded silently quantized, and now raises the existing inconsistent-scheme `ValueError` (whose message does not mention `.linear`);
- **mixing** plain and wrapped spellings previously raised, and now resolves to ignored.

`should_ignore_layer` is shared with `w8a8_int8.py`, where a 10-case probe moves only the three cases whose ignore list holds a `.linear` entry, and with diffusion `modelslim.py`, which passes a nested mapping and so never takes the fused path.

Tests are CPU-only and matcher-level: 10 cases, 5 red on main; the largest drives the checkpoint's 189-entry list at the tower's real runtime names. One checkpoint on one GPU, and no accuracy or throughput measurement.

#24929 identified this mechanism first; its hunk sits in `check_contains`, which the ignore path no longer reaches since #32736.
